root_cause: get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation resolve string (forward-ref) annotations against getattr(call, '__globals__'). For a functools.wraps wrapper defined in another module, __annotations__ is copied verbatim from the original function, but __globals__ belongs to the wrapper's module. So 'ForwardRefModel' is looked up in the wrong namespace: a NameError for params, and an unresolved ForwardRef response_model for the return annotation.
best_solution: Do what typing.get_type_hints does: follow __wrapped__ to the original function before reading __globals__. In both get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation, set unwrapped = inspect.unwrap(call) and use globalns = getattr(unwrapped, '__globals__', {}). Keep inspect.signature(call) as is, since signature already follows __wrapped__. inspect.unwrap handles chains of wrappers (the test double-wraps). The return-annotation function uses the same getattr(call, '__globals__') pattern and has to be fixed too, because FastAPI builds response_model from the return annotation.
acceptable_alternatives: A manual `while hasattr(f, '__wrapped__'): f = f.__wrapped__` loop is equivalent to inspect.unwrap, as long as it is applied in BOTH get_typed_signature and get_typed_return_annotation (or in one shared helper that both call).

The test registers passthrough(f) and passthrough(passthrough(f)) with app.post, then POSTs {'input': {'x': 0}} to both. Both responses must be {'x': 1}. The string return annotation must therefore resolve too, otherwise serialize_response raises PydanticUserError: TypeAdapter[Annotated[ForwardRef('ForwardRefModel'), ...]] is not fully defined.
locating_signals: The statement names get_typed_signature and globalns explicitly and points to typing.get_type_hints' __wrapped__ dereference. Its traceback leads to fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. The sibling get_typed_return_annotation is NOT named, but it sits a few lines below and uses the identical getattr(call, "__globals__", {}) line, so grepping __globals__ finds it. root_cause: In get_dependant(), `use_security_scopes = security_scopes or []` aliases the parent's scope list, then `use_security_scopes.extend(param_details.depends.scopes)` mutates it in place. Each Security() sub-dependency adds its scopes to the one list the parent and all siblings share, so scopes leak sideways (security2 also sees scope1, and vice versa) instead of flowing only from parent to child.
best_solution: Scopes are built into the Dependant tree once, at route registration (get_dependant recursion), not at request time. The statement says 'hierarchical propagation is broken', so read how get_dependant passes security_scopes down. The list is shared by reference and extended in place, which is the classic mutable-argument aliasing bug. Fix: build a new list instead of mutating: `use_security_scopes = use_security_scopes + list(param_details.depends.scopes)`. Each child then gets parent_scopes + own_scopes, and siblings stay independent (dep1 -> [scope3, scope1], dep2 -> [scope3, scope2]). Copying up front with `list(security_scopes or [])` before the extend works just as well.
acceptable_alternatives: Any non-mutating copy before extending: `use_security_scopes = list(security_scopes or [])` then extend (this is what our passing v8 patch did), or `[*security_scopes, *scopes]`. Changing solve_dependencies or SecurityScopes construction at request time does not fix this.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_security_scopes_dont_propagate.py::test_security_scopes_dont_propagate. A route has Security(dep3, scopes=['scope3']); dep3 has two sibling Security deps, security1 (scopes=['scope1']) and security2 (scopes=['scope2']), each returning SecurityScopes.scopes. GET /scopes must return exactly {'dep1': ['scope3','scope1'], 'dep2': ['scope3','scope2']}: parent scope first, then own scope, and no sibling leakage. Uses Annotated[..., Security(...)] syntax.
locating_signals: The statement is only a title plus 'see defect #5623'. 'security scope propagation' points to where Security scopes are threaded through the dependency tree: grep for `security_scopes` finds get_dependant in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, which contains the one `.extend(` on a list passed in by the parent. The function is not named in the statement. The linked issue text ('A case of parameter mutation in FastAPI causes leakage of added scopes to sibling dependencies') says outright that the bug is a mutation bug.
our_outcome_summary: Only v8 passed. v8 copied the list (`list(security_scopes) if security_scopes is not None else []`) before the extend, which is equivalent to gold. v4 produced an empty patch (35s, 23 calls). v6 patched the wrong layer: it added request-time scope propagation to solve_dependencies, passed a nonexistent `security_scopes=` kwarg to SolvedDependency and dropped `dependency_cache=`, which gave TypeError: SolvedDependency.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'security_scopes'. It also left the aliasing in get_dependant untouched. v7 made a cosmetic `scopes=dependant.security_scopes or []` change in solve_dependencies, which did not affect the leak (the test still saw sibling scopes), and it left a stray repro_scopes.py in the diff.
generalizable_lesson: When a bug is described as values 'leaking' or 'propagating wrongly' between siblings in a recursive tree build, first look for a mutable list/dict that is passed down and mutated in place (`x = arg or []` followed by `.append`/`.extend`/`[k]=`). Fix it with a copy (`x = list(arg or []) + new`) at that spot, not by adding new plumbing elsewhere. Also: when a statement is only 'see #N', fetch or infer the linked issue before editing. Never pass new kwargs to a dataclass or constructor without checking its fields. Never leave repro scripts in the final diff.

root_cause: With stringified annotations (from __future__ import annotations, or a literal -> "None"), the return annotation is the string "None". get_typed_annotation evaluates it via ForwardRef to NoneType (type(None)), not None. FastAPI then treats NoneType as a response_model, and APIRoute.__init__ asserts is_body_allowed_for_status_code, raising 'AssertionError: Status code 204 must not have a response body' at route registration.
best_solution: In fastapi/dependencies/utils.py get_typed_annotation, after evaluate_forwardref on a string annotation, add `if annotation is type(None): return None`. That maps an evaluated stringified None back to None, the same thing an unannotated or plain `-> None` route yields, so no response_model is inferred and 204 routes register. Checking the raw string (`annotation == "None"`) in get_typed_annotation or get_typed_return_annotation, before evaluation, also works for the test. The statement says the rule outright: if the return annotation is exactly "None", return None for the typed annotation.
acceptable_alternatives: Any of these pass the hidden test: return None early when the raw string annotation == "None" in get_typed_annotation (v4) or in get_typed_return_annotation (v6, v7). A check that covers only the non-string None object (`annotation is None`) does not.

locating_signals: The statement says 'return annotation of the route function', 'exactly "None"', 'typed annotation', '204 No Content'. 'typed annotation' leads to get_typed_annotation / get_typed_return_annotation in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py (grep 'typed_return_annotation'). The linked issue names fastapi.dependencies.utils.get_typed_return_annotation directly and shows the traceback into routing.py is_body_allowed_for_status_code. For anything touching annotations, test both the stringified form (from __future__ import annotations or a quoted annotation) and the plain form. Evaluating a string 'None' gives NoneType, not None. Before finishing, run a 3-line repro from the statement (define the route with the quoted annotation and status 204, then instantiate it). That would have exposed v8's miss at once.

root_cause: Dependant.is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable / is_coroutine_callable (cached properties in fastapi/dependencies/models.py) inspect self.call directly. A dependency decorated with a functools.wraps-style sync wrapper (or functools.cache's lru_cache_wrapper) is not itself a coroutine/generator function, so FastAPI classifies an async or generator dependency as a plain sync callable, runs it in the threadpool and injects the raw coroutine/generator object instead of awaiting/iterating it.
best_solution: Add a cached property `_unwrapped_call` returning `inspect.unwrap(self.call)` (returning self.call if it is None), and use it in place of self.call in all three classification properties (isgeneratorfunction, isasyncgenfunction, isroutine/iscoroutinefunction, isclass, and the `__call__` fallback). The call that is actually invoked stays self.call (the wrapper); only the type decision follows `__wrapped__` down to the real function, so a wrapper around an async def is awaited and a wrapper around a generator is driven as a context manager. The statement says 'in solve_dependencies', but at this base commit that logic had been refactored into the Dependant cached properties, so grep for isgeneratorfunction/iscoroutinefunction to find the real site.
acceptable_alternatives: Inline `call = inspect.unwrap(self.call)` at the top of each of the three properties (all four of our configs did this). Leaving isclass/dunder __call__ checks on self.call (v4) still passes; guarding None (v6) is optional since call is never None for these paths in tests.

Each dependency is decorated with a functools.wraps sync pass-through wrapper (noop_wrap); each route must return 200 with JSON body `true`. Sync-wrapper-around-async-def and around-async-generator are the cases that fail before the fix.
locating_signals: Statement names `inspect.unwrap`, `__wrapped__`, 'coroutine or (async) generator' and `solve_dependencies` (stale location). Grepping for iscoroutinefunction/isgeneratorfunction leads to Dependant.is_coroutine_callable etc. in fastapi/dependencies/models.py; the gold function is not named directly.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 all kaggle_env_pass=true; pod runs 63-99 s, 20-31 calls). Every patch inlined inspect.unwrap(self.call) in the three Dependant cached properties rather than adding a shared _unwrapped_call property; v4 only partially unwrapped is_coroutine_callable (isclass and dunder __call__ still on self.call) and v7 additionally unwrapped the dunder __call__, both harmless for the tests.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement names a function that no longer contains the described logic (code was refactored since the PR was written), grep for the primitive calls the statement describes (here inspect.iscoroutinefunction / isgeneratorfunction) and patch every sibling check consistently. For decorator/wrapper bugs, unwrap only for type classification (inspect.unwrap follows __wrapped__) while still invoking the original callable.
one_line_solution: Add _unwrapped_call = inspect.unwrap(self.call) and use it in all three Dependant is_*_callable properties.

root_cause: Dependant._unwrapped_call used only inspect.unwrap(self.call), which follows __wrapped__ but not functools.partial. The predicates is_coroutine_callable / is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable then inspect the partial object itself. inspect.isroutine(partial) is False and partial.__call__ is not a coroutine function, so partial(async_fn) was treated as sync and its un-awaited coroutine became the dependency value. For partial(callable_instance) the dunder lookup found partial.__call__ instead of the instance's __call__, so generator/async callable classes were misclassified. inspect.isgeneratorfunction/isasyncgenfunction already see through partials of plain functions, which is why those cases already worked.
best_solution: In fastapi/dependencies/models.py, Dependant._unwrapped_call: after unwrapped = inspect.unwrap(self.call), add `if isinstance(unwrapped, partial): unwrapped = unwrapped.func` (import partial from functools). Every sync/async/generator predicate reads _unwrapped_call, so this one normalization point fixes all of them: they now inspect the underlying function, bound method or callable instance, and the existing dunder-__call__ fallback works on the real instance. Signature and parameter extraction already handled partials, because inspect.signature drops the bound args. You can get to this from the statement alone: 'plain functions work, async and callable classes don't' points at sync/async classification rather than signature parsing, and grepping for iscoroutinefunction/isgeneratorfunction in fastapi/dependencies lands on these cached properties.
acceptable_alternatives: Loop `while isinstance(call, functools.partial): call = call.func` before or after inspect.unwrap (handles nested partials; this is what v4 did). A duck-typed hasattr(call, 'func') loop also passed (v8) but is fragile. Patching only get_typed_signature/get_typed_return_annotation in utils.py is NOT enough.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_dependency_partial.py::test_dependency_types_with_partial, parametrized over 12 routes. Each GET must return 200 with a JSON body equal to the string bound via partial. It covers Depends(partial(X, value)) where X is a sync function, async function, sync generator, async generator, callable instance (sync, sync-gen, async, async-gen __call__), and bound methods (sync, async, sync-gen, async-gen). No new API names. Behavior only.
locating_signals: The statement says 'dependables', 'functools.partial()', and 'partial of async and callable classes didn't work consistently'. It does not name the gold function (_unwrapped_call) or the file. The words 'async' and 'callable classes' point at the sync/async/generator classification on Dependant (is_coroutine_callable, is_gen_callable, is_async_gen_callable), all of which read _unwrapped_call. It passes but would wrongly unwrap any object that has a .func attribute. v6 (327s, 24 calls) produced an empty patch. v7 (94s, 53 calls) edited the wrong place: it unwrapped partials only in get_typed_signature/get_typed_return_annotation in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, which only affects the globalns used for annotation resolution, and left Dependant._unwrapped_call untouched. 5 of 12 tests failed with ResponseValidationError (the partial async function, callable-gen, async callable, async callable-gen and async method cases), because a coroutine or generator object was returned as the value. The 7 cases that inspect already handled passed.
generalizable_lesson: When a wrapper (functools.partial, a decorator, a callable instance) breaks behavior, first work out which predicate makes the wrong decision (here: sync vs async vs generator dispatch) and fix the single normalization helper that feeds all such predicates. Do not fix whatever helper you happened to grep first (signature/annotation parsing). Before editing, write a 10-line repro that covers the full combination matrix the statement implies (sync/async x function/generator x function/instance/method). Run it before and after the fix, and do not stop while any cell still fails. Also: an empty patch is always a loss, so when time runs short, submit the smallest plausible fix at the central helper.

root_cause: In _extract_form_body, _get_multidict_value returns None both for 'absent/empty' and for a None default, and values[field.alias] is only set when value is not None. The complement loop added by PR #12134 then copies every received_body key 'not in values' back in, so a declared Optional field sent as "" (treated as missing, default None, so skipped) gets re-added as the raw string "", which then fails int validation (422) or leaks "" instead of None.

Declared fields are then only ever populated by the first (default-aware) loop; extra undeclared keys still pass through for model-style forms. The statement says exactly this: 'keep track of already visited field, rather than relying on the content of the values dict', mirroring request_params_to_args.

root_cause: analyze_param() in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py only looks for Depends/Query/etc. metadata when get_origin(annotation) is Annotated. A PEP 695 alias (`type X = Annotated[int, Depends(f)]` or typing_extensions.TypeAliasType(...)) is a TypeAliasType object whose origin is not Annotated, so the Depends marker is never seen; the parameter is treated as a plain required query param and the request returns 422.
best_solution: At the top of analyze_param, before the `annotation is not inspect.Signature.empty` branch, unwrap the alias: `if is_typealiastype(annotation): annotation = annotation.__value__`, with `from typing_inspection.typing_objects import is_typealiastype`. Unwrapping once at the single entry point where parameter annotations are classified makes every downstream path (Annotated metadata scan for Depends/Query/Body, type_annotation, field creation) see the real `Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)]`. typing_inspection's helper is used because it matches both typing.TypeAliasType and typing_extensions.TypeAliasType (which are distinct classes on Python < 3.14), which is the edge case Viicos flagged on the earlier PR #11140. Reasoning path from the statement: reproduce with the issue example, observe 422 (param became a query param), grep where Annotated metadata is extracted for params (`get_origin(annotation) is Annotated` in dependencies/utils.py analyze_param), unwrap the alias there.

best_solution: Stop depending on either Starlette constant name: replace every use with the literal value. In fastapi/exception_handlers.py drop HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY from the starlette.status import (keep WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION) and use status_code=422 in request_validation_exception_handler. In fastapi/openapi/utils.py remove the import line and change `http422 = str(HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)` to `http422 = "422"` in get_openapi_path. Same change in docs_src/handling_errors/tutorial005.py (drop `status` import, status_code=422). Upstream also bumped pyproject starlette range to <0.49.0 (stripped from the gold patch). Works on both old and new Starlette with no warnings; `grep -rn HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` must return only tests after the change.

hidden_test_demands: tests/test_enforce_once_required_parameter.py: test_get_invalid asserts response.status_code == 422 (literal); test_schema fetches /openapi.json, which runs get_openapi_path and needs the 422 response key "422" with no NameError/DeprecationWarning; test_get_valid. No new API names or strings beyond the integer 422 / string "422".
locating_signals: Statement names both constants HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY / HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT and says 'updated all instances' to literal 422/"422"; a repo-wide grep for HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY finds exactly the gold sites (exception_handlers.py import+use, openapi/utils.py import+use, docs_src tutorial). root_cause: APIRouter.include_router(router) had no identity check, so router.include_router(router) iterated over its own routes list while appending to it, hanging the process (discussion 14251: 'Locks program'). The method validated its other arguments with assert statements but never checked `router is self`.
best_solution: At the top of APIRouter.include_router in fastapi/routing.py, right after the docstring and before the existing `if prefix: assert prefix.startswith('/')` checks, add `assert self is not router, ("Cannot include the same APIRouter instance into itself. Did you mean to include a different router?")`. It uses assert (AssertionError) because every other argument check in that method is an assert, and it runs before any route is copied, so the self-include loop never starts.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_router_circular_import.py::test_router_circular_import: router = APIRouter(); pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="Cannot include the same APIRouter instance into itself. Did you mean to include a different router?") around router.include_router(router). Exception type must be AssertionError (not FastAPIError/ValueError), and because match uses re.search the message must contain that exact sentence pair. The earlier closed PR 11425 used a different message ('Router cannot be the same as parent'), so no linked source contains the final string.
locating_signals: The title 'include router into itself' points straight at APIRouter.include_router in fastapi/routing.py (the function is named in effect, not verbatim). The existing assert-based prefix validation at the top of that method shows which exception type to use. The statement gives no message text; only the linked discussions/PR (not visible offline) describe the hang and a `router is self` check.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 (369s, 11 calls) and v8 (32s, 16 calls) produced empty patches. v7 (198s, 109 calls) wrote only a root-level test_circular_router.py with no source change, so nothing in routing.py changed. v6 (379s, 32 calls) came closest: it put the guard in the right place (`if router is self: raise FastAPIError("Cannot include a router into itself")`), but the hidden test expects AssertionError with the exact gold message, so it failed with an uncaught FastAPIError (log: fastapi/routing.py:1397 FastAPIError). v6 went wrong twice. It raised a custom exception instead of copying the method's existing assert idiom, and it chose its own message wording.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement asks for a 'clear error' guard in a method that already validates its arguments, copy that method's existing mechanism exactly: if the neighbouring checks are `assert cond, "msg"`, add another assert (AssertionError), not a custom exception class. Hidden tests usually pytest.raises the idiom already in use. Put the guard first, before any side effects. Write a full, explicit message that reuses the statement's wording and names the class (e.g., 'Cannot include the same <Class> instance into itself'). Never submit an empty or test-only patch: a feature or bugfix statement always needs a source change, so check that git diff touches non-test files before finishing.
acceptable_alternatives: Any AssertionError-raising check placed before route copying passes only if its message contains the exact gold string, because the test uses re.search with the full sentence. Different wording, or FastAPIError/ValueError/RecursionError, fails. An assert with a guessed message would fix the exception type but still fail the match, so the task can't be solved without the hidden string.

root_cause: get_parameterless_sub_dependant() (used for dependencies=[Depends(...)] on routes, routers and the app) called get_dependant(path, call, security_scopes) without forwarding depends.scope, so Depends(f, scope='function') at those levels fell back to the default 'request' scope and the yield-teardown ran after the response instead of before it.
best_solution: In fastapi/dependencies/utils.py get_parameterless_sub_dependant, pass scope=depends.scope into the get_dependant(...) call alongside path, call and security_scopes. get_dependant already accepts a scope kwarg (the parametered sub-dependency path already forwards it), so the parameterless path simply has to thread the same attribute through. With scope='function' the exit code after yield now runs inside the endpoint's exit stack, so an HTTPException raised after yield becomes a 503 response; with scope='request' it still runs after the response is sent (client sees 200).
acceptable_alternatives: Any call ordering of the kwargs; forwarding scope positionally is not possible (keyword-only). Nothing else needed.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_dependency_yield_scope.py adds test_router_level_dep_scope_function (include_router(dependencies=[Depends(raise_after_yield, scope='function')]) -> 503 {'detail': 'Exception after yield'}), test_router_level_dep_scope_request (-> 200 {'status': 'ok'} with raise_server_exceptions=False), test_app_level_dep_scope_function (FastAPI(dependencies=[...scope='function']) -> 503), test_app_level_dep_scope_request (-> 200). No new API; only behavior of existing Depends(scope=...).
locating_signals: Statement names the exact function get_parameterless_sub_dependant, the target get_dependant, and the missing attribute depends.scope. grep for get_parameterless_sub_dependant lands on the one-line fix.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all: v4, v6, v7, v8 all pass in the Kaggle env (11 passed). v4/v6/v7 produced the identical one-line patch (scope=depends.scope appended to the get_dependant call), 36-83s, 12-22 calls. v8 made the same source fix plus an extra tests/test_issue_repro.py file (2064 chars, 51 calls, 111s); the extra test file was harmless but wasted calls.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says a value 'is not forwarded/passed through' in a named helper, find that helper's call to the downstream function, compare its kwargs against sibling call sites that already forward the attribute, and add the one missing keyword; do not refactor or add repro test files once the one-line forward is in place.
one_line_solution: Pass scope=depends.scope into get_dependant from get_parameterless_sub_dependant.

root_cause: Feature, not a bug: ValidationException subclasses (RequestValidationError, WebSocketRequestValidationError, ResponseValidationError) carried only the error list, and only ResponseValidationError had a __str__ (always plural 'validation errors'). Nothing recorded which endpoint raised the error, so server-side tracebacks could not point at the handler.
best_solution:
In fastapi/exceptions.py add a TypedDict EndpointContext(total=False) with function/path/file/line. Give ValidationException.__init__(errors, *, endpoint_ctx=None), store it plus endpoint_function/path/file/line attributes, and move __str__ up into the base class: '<n> validation error' plus 's' only when n != 1, then one '  {err}' line per error, then a context block. If file, line and function are all known, append '
  File "<file>", line <line>, in <function>' followed by '
    <path>' when a path exists. If only the path is known, append '
  Endpoint: <path>'. Otherwise append nothing. rstrip the result. All three subclasses accept and forward endpoint_ctx as a keyword. In fastapi/routing.py add _extract_endpoint_context(func), cached by id(func), that uses inspect.getsourcefile/getsourcelines/__name__ inside a try/except. In get_request_handler's inner app, and in get_websocket_app, build the ctx from dependant.call and set ctx['path'] = f'{request.method} {root_path.rstrip("/")}{dependant.path}' (or 'WS ...' for websockets). The route template plus root_path is what makes mounted sub-apps show '/sub/items/'. Pass endpoint_ctx= into every RequestValidationError / WebSocketRequestValidationError raise, and thread a new endpoint_ctx kwarg through serialize_response to the ResponseValidationError raise.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_validation_error_context.py (7 tests). It constructs RequestValidationError(errors, endpoint_ctx={'path': 'GET /api/test'}) directly and asserts 'Endpoint: GET /api/test' in str(exc) and 'File "' not in it. It constructs RequestValidationError(errors, endpoint_ctx={}) and asserts '1 validation error:' (singular) with no 'Endpoint' or 'File "'. Through a TestClient with exception handlers registered on app and on a mounted sub_app at /sub, str(exc) must contain the function name and route for: a request path-param error (get_user, '/users/'), a response_model error (get_item, '/items/'), a websocket path-param error (websocket_endpoint, '/ws/'), a sub-app response error (get_sub_item, '/sub/items/') and a sub-app websocket error (subapp_websocket_endpoint, '/sub/ws/'). The kwarg name endpoint_ctx (a dict), the 'Endpoint: ' fallback format and the singular/plural rule never appear as names in the statement.
locating_signals: The statement names the three exception classes (RequestValidationError, ResponseValidationError, WebSocketRequestValidationError), which leads to fastapi/exceptions.py, and the 'Before/After' str() output shows the exact File/line/in format and the 'METHOD /route' line. 'extracted once per endpoint and then cached' points to the request handler factories in routing.py (get_request_handler, get_websocket_app, serialize_response). No function or parameter is named. The key name endpoint_ctx, the TypedDict and the path-only fallback are hidden.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 got 3/7: it added an endpoint_context: str kwarg (the tests call endpoint_ctx=dict, so TypeError on the 2 direct-construction tests), kept the plural 'validation errors' text, and in get_request_handler passed endpoint=route.endpoint, method=scope['method'] to serialize_response even though neither route nor scope exists in that closure. That raised a NameError instead of ResponseValidationError, so the handler never captured anything on /items/ and /sub/items/. It also left junk test.py/test_context.py files in the repo root. v6 inserted an @lru_cache def into the middle of the 'from fastapi.exceptions import (' statement in routing.py, which is a SyntaxError (unmatched ')'), so collection failed. It also lru_cached on (dependant, request), which is unhashable/per-request, and referenced an undefined endpoint_context in serialize_response. v7 wrote literal backslash-escaped quotes (f\"...\") into exceptions.py (SyntaxError), never touched routing.py, and left a duplicate __str__ in place. v8 produced only a scratch test_exceptions.py with no source change, so all 7 tests failed.
generalizable_lesson: When a feature's tests will construct your new exception or object directly, the keyword name is the API. Pick the name the statement's wording implies, and when the statement gives an exact str() rendering, copy it character for character, including singular/plural ('1 validation error:'). Build a rendering that degrades gracefully when fields are missing. Prefer a dict/TypedDict context over a pre-formatted string so partial data still renders. Only thread values that are actually in scope in the closure you are editing: read the enclosing function signature before referencing route/scope/request. After any edit to an import block or string literals, run python -m py_compile on the file, and delete scratch files before finishing. Two of four runs died on SyntaxErrors that a compile check would have caught in one second.
acceptable_alternatives: Any object type works for endpoint_ctx as long as it accepts a dict with optional function/path/file/line keys. The cache can be keyed on the function object or on id(func), or computed once at route-build time in APIRoute.__init__ and closed over. The path must be the route template (dependant.path or route.path) prefixed with the mount root_path, not the concrete request URL, although tests only check substrings like '/users/' and '/sub/items/', so request.url.path would also pass. ValidationException.__str__ must live on the base class so request and websocket errors render context too.
one_line_solution: Add an endpoint_ctx (TypedDict) kwarg to the ValidationException family, a singular/plural __str__ in the base, and pass the context from routing.

root_cause: Depends and Security had been turned into plain @dataclass classes. A dataclass with eq=True and no frozen/unsafe_hash gets __hash__ = None, so hash(Depends(dep)) raised TypeError. That broke third-party tools such as Cadwyn, which relied on the objects being hashable (closed PR 14320). The obvious fix, frozen=True, has a knock-on effect: analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py does `depends = copy(depends); depends.dependency = type_annotation` for the `x: Foo = Depends()` / `Annotated[Foo, Depends()]` class shortcut, and that line raises FrozenInstanceError once the class is frozen.
best_solution: In fastapi/params.py change `@dataclass` to `@dataclass(frozen=True)` on both Depends and its subclass Security. With eq=True, frozen=True makes Python generate a value-based __hash__ over the fields (dependency, use_cache, scope, plus scopes for Security), so equal instances hash equal and a different scope hashes differently. Then grep for code that mutates instances: analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py assigns `depends.dependency = type_annotation` on a copy. Replace that with `depends = dataclasses.replace(depends, dependency=type_annotation)` and add `import dataclasses`. The patch also has to cover the mutation site, or the class-as-dependency shortcut breaks at route definition time.
acceptable_alternatives: `@dataclass(unsafe_hash=True)` on both classes passes the hidden test and keeps the objects mutable, so utils.py needs no change (this was option 2 in PR 14320). An explicit `__hash__` over (dependency, use_cache, scope[, scopes]) also works. Option 3 from PR 14320 (identity hash via object.__hash__) fails, because the test asserts hash(Depends(dep)) == hash(Depends(dep)) for two distinct instances. frozen=True without the dataclasses.replace change passes the hidden test but breaks `Depends()` with no argument.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_depends_hashable.py::test_depends_hashable: hash(Depends(dep)) == hash(Depends(dep)); hash(Security(dep)) == hash(Security(dep)); hash(Depends(dep)) != hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')); hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')) == hash(Depends(dep, scope='function')). So the hash must be value-based (identity hash fails) and must include the scope field. Only default scopes=None is exercised for Security. The hidden test does not cover the `Depends()` no-argument path.
locating_signals: The title names `Depends()` and `Security()`. Grepping `class Depends` finds fastapi/params.py, where both are bare `@dataclass`. That, plus the dataclass rule that eq without frozen sets __hash__ = None, gives the main fix. The second gold location (analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, `depends.dependency = type_annotation`) is not named anywhere. You only find it by grepping for assignments to Depends fields after freezing the class, or by running the existing suite (e.g. the tests for classes used as dependencies with `Depends()`).
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6, v7 and v8 all passed in the Kaggle env (47-84s, 12-23 calls). All four only changed the two decorators in fastapi/params.py to @dataclass(frozen=True). v8 also added a Security.__post_init__ that converts scopes to a tuple via object.__setattr__. None of them updated analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, which still runs `depends.dependency = type_annotation` on a frozen copy. That raises FrozenInstanceError for `x: Foo = Depends()` / `Annotated[Foo, Depends()]` (checked: assigning a field on a copied frozen dataclass raises `FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'dependency'`). The patches passed only because the grader runs just the hidden test file (log: 1 passed). If the full suite ran, they would regress.
generalizable_lesson: If you make a class immutable or hashable (dataclass frozen=True, NamedTuple, __slots__ with read-only properties), grep the whole package for attribute assignments on its instances (`\.<field>\s*=`, setattr, `copy(x); x.f = ...`) and rewrite them as dataclasses.replace(...) or a constructor call. Then run the existing tests that touch that class, not just the new one. For a 'make X hashable' request on a dataclass, remember that eq=True without frozen sets __hash__ = None. Choose frozen=True (value hash, but you must fix mutation sites) or unsafe_hash=True (value hash, stays mutable). Tests usually assert that equal-field instances hash equal, so an identity hash is not enough.
one_line_solution: @dataclass(frozen=True) on Depends and Security (and replace the in-place `depends.dependency =` with dataclasses.replace).
statement_title: ♻️ Make the result of `Depends()` and `Security()` hashable, as a workaround for other tools interacting with these internal parts

root_cause: Dependant.cache_key always included tuple(sorted(set(self.security_scopes))), and security_scopes was inherited from every Security(..., scopes=...) ancestor. So a plain dependency such as get_db reached through Security(get_user, scopes=['read']) got key (get_db, ('read',)) while the direct Depends(get_db) got (get_db, ()), and the per-request cache ran it twice even though get_db never looks at scopes.
best_solution: Make scopes part of the cache key only when the dependency actually uses them, transitively. In fastapi/dependencies/models.py add a cached_property `_uses_scopes` that is True if the dependant declared its own Security scopes, or has a SecurityScopes parameter (security_scopes_param_name is not None), or any sub-dependant has `_uses_scopes`. Then cache_key = (call, tuple(sorted(set(oauth_scopes))) if self._uses_scopes else (), computed_scope or ''). To tell 'declared own scopes' apart from 'inherited scopes', gold splits the old security_scopes field into own_oauth_scopes and parent_oauth_scopes, with an `oauth_scopes` property that merges parent then own (order preserved, deduped). get_dependant/get_parameterless_sub_dependant in utils.py pass own_oauth_scopes from the Security marker and parent_oauth_scopes=current_scopes to children. SecurityScopes injection and the dependency-override path use oauth_scopes, and SecurityRequirement gets current_scopes for any SecurityBase. A smaller fix should also pass the hidden tests (traced by hand, not run): keep security_scopes and compute _uses_scopes = security_scopes_param_name is not None or any(sub._uses_scopes for sub in self.dependencies). The recursion over sub-dependencies is the part that matters.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_security_scopes.py::test_security_scopes_dependency_called_once: endpoint has Depends(get_db) and Security(get_user, scopes=['read']) where get_user depends on get_db; get_db must run exactly once. tests/test_security_scopes_sub_dependency.py::test_security_scopes_sub_dependency_caching: get_current_user(SecurityScopes, Depends(get_db_session)), get_user_me = Security(get_current_user, scopes=['me']), get_user_items = Depends(get_user_me), endpoint uses Depends(get_user_me) and Security(get_user_items, scopes=['items']). Expected counts: get_db_session 1, get_current_user 2, get_user_me 2, get_user_items 1. The exact JSON shows the second get_current_user sees scopes ['items','me'] (parent first, then own) and both share db_session_1. So scope-reading deps and their ancestors stay keyed by scopes, and scope-free leaves are shared.
locating_signals: The title and last paragraph ('Dependencies are cached based on the function. And also on the scopes, but only when ... this dependency or a sub-dependency declare scopes or access the SecurityScopes') state the rule exactly. Searching for 'cache' plus 'scopes' leads to Dependant.cache_key in fastapi/dependencies/models.py, which the statement does not name. The words 'or by a sub-dependency' are the signal that the check must recurse. The linked discussion diagrams are not visible offline.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4 (103s, 43 calls) came closest: in cache_key it kept the scopes only when self.security_scopes_param_name was set. That fixed test_security_scopes (get_db called once), but the check was not transitive. get_user_me has no SecurityScopes parameter of its own, yet its sub-dependency get_current_user does, so v4 merged both get_user_me calls into one cache entry (log: assert 1 == 2 on get_user_me). v6 (90s, 26 calls) went the opposite way and appended the sub-dependants' cache keys to the tuple. Keys got more specific, not less, so get_db still ran twice (2 == 1 in both tests). v7 (173s, 41 calls) produced an empty patch. v8 (143s, 51 calls) edited the wrong place: it only added `sub_dependant.use_cache and` to the cache-store condition in solve_dependencies and left cache_key alone, so both tests failed with 2 == 1. v4 and v8 also added stray test files (v8 at the repo root).
generalizable_lesson: When a statement gives a rule with a recursive clause ('this X or any of its sub-Xs does Y'), implement it as a memoized recursive predicate over the child graph, not a check on the node's own fields only. Then build the statement's own nested example (parent -> child -> grandchild that does Y) as a quick test before you finish. For cache-key or dedup bugs where something runs too often, the fix is to remove or conditionally drop a key component. Adding more components (v6) can only split the cache further. Check the direction with a call counter before submitting.
acceptable_alternatives: The minimal version keeps the existing security_scopes field and adds a recursive `_uses_scopes` (security_scopes_param_name set, or any sub-dependant uses scopes) used to include or drop scopes in cache_key. By hand trace (not executed) it satisfies both hidden tests, because inherited-scope order is already parent then own. The own/parent split in gold is only needed to count 'declared its own Security scopes' as usage.
one_line_solution: Keep scopes in Dependant.cache_key only when the dependant or any sub-dependant (transitive, memoized) uses SecurityScopes.

root_cause: Since 0.123.5 Dependant.is_coroutine_callable / is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable classified a callable only by its innermost target (inspect.unwrap(call), then strip one partial). An async @wraps wrapper around a sync function was therefore treated as sync, and its coroutine was never awaited ('coroutine' object is not iterable). Two more gaps: a callable instance whose __call__ method is itself decorated was never unwrapped, and a callable that is both a sync generator (inner) and an async generator (wrapper) went down the sync contextmanager path, because _solve_generator tested is_gen_callable first.
best_solution: Add module helpers _impartial(f), which strips nested functools.partial layers, and _unwrapped_call(f) = inspect.unwrap(_impartial(f)). In each of the three flags, test both the outer callable (partial-stripped) and its fully unwrapped target, then do the same for its __call__ (the __call__ of the partial-stripped callable, and the __call__ of the unwrapped one), and return True if any level matches. The rule is 'async at any layer means await it', because an async wrapper around sync code, or a sync wrapper around async code, both give back something awaitable. Keep the default of False for classes. Because a wrapped callable can now be both a gen and an async gen, reorder _solve_generator in utils.py to check is_async_gen_callable before is_gen_callable (asynccontextmanager first).
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_dependency_wrapped.py::test_class_dependency, parametrized over 28 routes, each of which must return 200 with body true. It covers sync noop_wrap and async noop_wrap_async wrappers around: plain functions, gens and async gens; callable instances (wrapped instance, or a decorated __call__ that is sync/async/gen/async-gen); classes; and endpoints themselves. The key cases: a class instance with @noop_wrap async __call__ (the bound __call__ must be unwrapped); @noop_wrap def __call__ that yields, sync or async (same); and @noop_wrap_async over a sync gen, which gives an async-gen wrapper around a sync gen, so the async-gen branch has to win in _solve_generator. No new public API.
locating_signals: The statement says 'functools wraps and partial', 'async, generator, async generator, callable instance', and 'analyze the function but also the wrapper'. grep for inspect.unwrap / partial / isgeneratorfunction finds Dependant._unwrapped_call and the is_*_callable cached properties in fastapi/dependencies/models.py. The statement never names the second location, the gen-vs-async-gen dispatch order in _solve_generator (fastapi/dependencies/utils.py); you only reach it by tracing how the flags are consumed.
our_outcome_summary: Failed on all 4 configs (v4/v6/v7/v8). v6, v7 and v8 each scored 24/28. They walked the partial/__wrapped__ chain of self.call and checked each node and node.__call__, but they never unwrapped the bound __call__ method. That failed class-instance-async-wrapped, class-instance-wrapped-gen and class-instance-async-wrapped-gen. None of them touched utils.py, so wrapped-gen-dependency-async-wrapper (async-gen wrapper around a sync gen) still went through contextmanager and failed. v4 (558s, 47 calls) produced no pytest output at all. Its _is_any_async loop follows current = current.__call__ whenever hasattr(__call__) is true. Each access returns a fresh method-wrapper, so the loop never ends for a non-matching callable, and app construction at import hung until timeout. v4 also left a stray test_async_callable.py at the repo root.
generalizable_lesson: When fixing a type-classification predicate (is async / is generator / is callable), list every indirection layer the input can have: wrapper, wrapped, partial, instance, the instance's __call__, and a decorated __call__. Apply the full normalization at every layer, and write a quick matrix script over those combinations before stopping. Then grep every consumer of the predicates. If two flags can now both be true, the if/elif order where they are used decides the behavior and may need to change, and that consumer can live in another file. Never write a loop over getattr(x, '__call__'): it never reaches a fixed point, so bound it or check identity.
acceptable_alternatives: Any normalization that checks every layer works: the outer callable, each partial.func, each __wrapped__, and the __call__ of every one of those, itself unwrapped through inspect.unwrap on the bound method. It must also reorder async-gen before gen in _solve_generator, or make is_gen_callable return False whenever an async-gen layer exists. The loop has to terminate, for example by using inspect.unwrap plus a bounded __call__ step, not an unbounded __call__ walk.
one_line_solution: Classify async/generator at every wrapper layer (partial, __wrapped__, instance, __call__, decorated __call__); prefer the async-gen path in _solve_generator.
statement_title: 🐛 Fix support for functools wraps and partial combined, for async and regular functions and classes in path operations and dependencies
v4_blocker: own infinite loop over __call__ hung import (558 s)
flip_note: Hard: seven indirection layers plus a consumer in another file.

root_cause: FastAPI 0.123.6 changed Dependant.is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable / is_coroutine_callable to fall back to inspecting getattr(call, '__call__'). When the dependency is a class (Depends() on a class annotation) whose instances define an async/generator __call__, the class's __call__ attribute is that unbound function, so the class itself was misclassified as a coroutine/generator. FastAPI then awaited or iterated the class constructor result instead of just instantiating it.
best_solution: In each of the three is_*_callable cached properties in fastapi/dependencies/models.py, after the direct function checks on self.call and before the dunder_call fallback, add `if inspect.isclass(_unwrapped_call(self.call)): return False`. A class is called to build an instance; calling it is synchronous and never yields, whatever its instances' __call__ looks like. Also drop the stale comment that said the class case was covered by the default return. The statement names the three methods and the check, so the fix follows directly from it.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_dependency_class.py::test_class_dependency gets four new parametrized routes: /callable-dependency-class, /callable-gen-dependency-class, /async-callable-dependency-class and /async-callable-gen-dependency-class. Each uses `instance: <Class> = Depends()` with CallableDependency, CallableGenDependency, AsyncCallableDependency or AsyncCallableGenDependency, and the handler calls the instance itself. The injected value must be an instance of the class, not an awaited or iterated __call__ result. No new API or exact string is required.
locating_signals: The statement names the exact functions (is_coroutine_callable, is_async_gen_callable, is_gen_callable), the concept dunder_call, and the fix (check whether the callable is a class before inspecting dunder_call). Grepping for dunder_call or is_gen_callable leads straight to fastapi/dependencies/models.py.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) passed in the Kaggle env, in 68-90s with 17-23 calls. v8 is the closest to gold: isclass(_impartial(self.call)) at the same three points. v4 also adds a redundant second isclass check on _unwrapped_call before dunder_unwrapped_call. That is harmless. v6 uses isclass(self.call) with no unwrapping, which would miss a functools.partial of a class, and it leaves a stray test file behind. v7 puts the check after the `dunder_call is None` guard and leaves a reproduce_issue.py script in the repo. Both still pass the hidden tests.
generalizable_lesson: When a type-detection helper falls back to inspecting obj.__call__, guard against classes first with inspect.isclass: a class's __call__ attribute is its instances' method, not how the class itself behaves when called. More generally, when the statement is a PR description naming the functions and the check to add, apply that exact check at the same point in every function it lists, unwrap the object the same way the nearby code does (partial or wrapped), and delete scratch reproduce and test files before finishing.
acceptable_alternatives: Using isclass on self.call, _impartial(self.call) or _unwrapped_call(self.call) all pass. Putting the check after the dunder_call None-guard (v7) also passes. The only requirement is that it runs before the dunder_call coroutine/generator inspection in all three methods.
one_line_solution: `if inspect.isclass(_unwrapped_call(self.call)): return False` in all three is_*_callable properties, before the __call__ fallback.
statement_title: 🐛 Fix using class (not instance) dependency that has `__call__` method

root_cause: In get_openapi_path, each route's additional response dict is copied with a shallow dict.copy(); the nested 'content' dict is therefore shared with route.responses. App-level FastAPI(responses=...) makes every route share that same dict, so deep_dict_update merging the generated Union schema into process_response['content'][media_type] mutates the shared source, and each subsequent route appends another copy of the anyOf $refs.
best_solution: Replace `process_response = additional_response.copy()` with `process_response = copy.deepcopy(additional_response)` (plus `import copy`) in fastapi/openapi/utils.py get_openapi_path. A deep copy detaches the nested content/schema dicts from route.responses, so deep_dict_update only mutates a per-route throwaway and the shared app-level config stays pristine; every route gets exactly [ModelA, ModelB] in anyOf. The statement points at the exact line (shallow .copy()) and the mutation mechanism.
acceptable_alternatives: Deep-copying only the 'content' sub-dict, or building a fresh dict before deep_dict_update, would also pass; making deep_dict_update non-mutating (return a new dict) works too but touches a shared helper. Deduplicating anyOf entries would hide the symptom but still leak mutation into route.responses (and still grow the title/other merged keys).
hidden_test_demands: New file tests/test_additional_responses_union_duplicate_anyof.py::test_openapi_schema: app-level responses={500: {model: Union[ModelA, ModelB], content: {application/json: {examples: {...}}}}} with two routes; asserts the full /openapi.json equals an exact dict where each route's 500 schema has anyOf of exactly two $refs (ModelA, ModelB), a per-route title ('Response 500 Route1 Route1 Get' / 'Response 500 Route2 Route2 Get'), and the examples preserved.
locating_signals: Statement is the PR description and names the file (fastapi/openapi/utils.py), line range, the exact expression `additional_response.copy()` described as 'shallowly copied', and deep_dict_update as the mutator. Function get_openapi_path is implied by the linked snippet. Fix is effectively spelled out.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 all kaggle_env_pass=true). Every agent patch applies the identical one-line change to copy.deepcopy plus import copy. v4/v7/v8 also left a stray reproduce_issue.py at repo root (harmless here). Pod cost: v6 fastest (62s, 20 calls), v8 slowest (176s, 48 calls) for the same patch.
generalizable_lesson: When a function builds per-item output from a shared config dict (app-level defaults, class attributes, module constants) and then merges into it with an in-place helper, a shallow .copy() leaks mutation across iterations; symptoms are output that grows with the number of items (duplicates accumulating in lists). Fix at the copy site with copy.deepcopy rather than deduplicating downstream. Also: clean up scratch reproduce scripts before finishing.
one_line_solution: copy.deepcopy (not dict.copy) the per-route additional response in get_openapi_path.
statement_title: 🐛 Fix OpenAPI duplication of `anyOf` refs for app-level responses with specified `content` and `model` as `Union`

root_cause: _get_multidict_value in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py calls values.getlist(alias) whenever is_sequence_field(field) is true and the source is an ImmutableMultiDict or Headers. Pydantic v2 turns Json[list[str]] into Annotated[list[str], Json()]. FieldInfo keeps the stripped annotation list[str] and puts a Json() instance in field_info.metadata. So FastAPI saw a sequence field and passed ['["abc","def"]'] (a list) to a validator that needs a JSON string, which gave 422 'JSON input should be string, bytes or bytearray'. This hits Form, Query and Header. Cookie is unaffected because cookies are a plain dict.
best_solution: Import Json from pydantic and add a helper `_is_json_field(field) -> bool: return any(type(item) is Json for item in field.field_info.metadata)`. In _get_multidict_value, add `(not _is_json_field(field)) and` in front of the is_sequence_field/isinstance condition, so Json-wrapped fields take the `values.get(alias)` branch and Pydantic receives the raw JSON string. The statement already shows the getlist-to-get swap. The part it leaves out is how to detect Json: the marker is an instance in metadata, not a class and not in the annotation, so the check needs type()/isinstance, not `Json in metadata` or `arg is Json`. Putting the check in the shared multidict reader fixes every multidict source at once.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_json_type.py with four endpoints typed Annotated[Json[list[str]], X()] for X = Form, Query, Header (x_items / 'x-items') and Cookie. Each sends json.dumps(['abc','def']) and asserts status 200 and body == ['abc','def']. test_form_json_list, test_query_json_list and test_header_json_list fail at base. test_cookie_json_list already passes. The statement only mentions Form(), but Query and Header are tested too, so a Form-only fix fails 2 of 4 (seen in race1 r_v4). The module needs python-multipart installed or collection fails.
locating_signals: The statement names the mechanism: 'treated it as a sequence field and used getlist()', with before/after snippets of values.getlist("items") vs values.get("items"). Grepping getlist( leads straight to _get_multidict_value in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. The closing line 'metadata attribute does not exist in Pydantic v1's FieldInfo' hints that detection should read field.field_info.metadata. The function name itself does not appear in the statement.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. No patch's Json check ever evaluates true, so every patch leaves the behavior unchanged. v6 (112s, 63 calls) edited the right spot, _get_multidict_value, but tested `Json in field.field_info.metadata`. metadata holds a Json() instance, and Json() does not compare equal to the Json class, so the check is always False. That was one expression away from gold (`type(item) is Json`). v4 (210s, 106 calls) changed _compat/v2.is_sequence_field to look for Annotated/Json in field.field_info.annotation. Pydantic has already stripped that annotation to list[str], so the check does nothing. v7 (214s, 91 calls) and v8 (168s, 109 calls) added Annotated handling to _compat/shared.field_annotation_is_sequence. That function receives the stripped annotation too, so the new branch never runs. v8's `arg is Json` would also miss the instance. v7 matched on __name__/str(), which an instance does not satisfy. All four also left repro/test files in the diff. Pod eval3 logs can't be used here: python-multipart is missing, so collection errors even for the oracle (oracle_all hit a pydantic IncEx ImportError). The Kaggle result is the one to trust.
generalizable_lesson: When a fix depends on spotting a library type wrapper (typing.Annotated markers, pydantic Json/constr/Field, dataclass fields), don't guess how the library represents it. Build the real object in a one-line REPL and print it, e.g. FieldInfo.from_annotation(Json[list[str]]).annotation and .metadata. Libraries often strip Annotated and store markers as instances, so `Marker in metadata`, `arg is Marker` and `get_origin(ann) is Marker` all fail silently. Use isinstance(m, Marker) or type(m) is Marker on the stored metadata. Then run the statement's repro and confirm it goes from failing to passing. If the repro can't run because an optional dependency is missing (e.g. python-multipart for forms), test the same code path through another entry point (query/header) rather than skipping the check. Put the fix at the shared chokepoint the statement names (here the getlist call) so every caller gets it. Hidden tests often cover sibling entry points (Query, Header, Cookie) that the statement never mentions.
acceptable_alternatives: Any check that sees the Json() instance in field.field_info.metadata (isinstance(m, Json), type(m) is Json, or type(m).__name__ == 'Json') and makes _get_multidict_value use values.get works. Making is_sequence_field return False for such fields also works, if it reads metadata and not annotation. Limiting the check to params.Form fails the Query/Header tests.
one_line_solution: In _get_multidict_value skip getlist when any field_info.metadata item is a Json() instance (`type(item) is Json`).

root_cause: get_authorization_scheme_param() splits the Authorization header with str.partition(" ") and returns the remainder verbatim, so extra spaces between scheme and token ("Bearer   xxx") or trailing whitespace ("Bearer xxx ") stay in the credentials string, violating RFC 6750 where spaces are only separators.
best_solution: In fastapi/security/utils.py, change `return scheme, param` to `return scheme, param.strip()`. Every security scheme (HTTPBase, HTTPBearer, OAuth2 bearer variants) routes through this one helper, so stripping the post-partition remainder fixes leading multi-space and trailing whitespace for all of them at once; scheme stays unchanged and empty/missing headers still return ("", "").
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_security_http_base.py::test_security_http_base_with_whitespaces sends 'Authorization: Other  foobar ' and expects 200 with {"scheme": "Other", "credentials": "foobar"}; tests/test_security_oauth2_authorization_code_bearer.py::test_token_with_whitespaces sends 'Bearer  testtoken ' and expects {"token": "testtoken"}. Both require stripping both leading (double space) and trailing whitespace from the credential.
locating_signals: Statement names the function get_authorization_scheme_param() and the file fastapi/security/utils.py and gives the exact one-line diff `return scheme, param.strip()`. Keywords: Authorization header, credentials, HTTPBearer.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass true). All four agent patches are byte-identical to the gold patch (404 chars), in 43-55 s and 14-20 tool calls on the pod.
generalizable_lesson: When the problem statement is a PR description that already contains the code change (a 'Solution' snippet plus a 'Changes' bullet naming function and file), apply exactly that edit in the named shared helper rather than patching individual callers; fixing the single chokepoint makes every caller's hidden tests pass, and extra caller-level changes only add risk.

Stripping only leading spaces would fail both hidden tests because they include a trailing space. Changing the scheme to be case-normalized or stripping inside each security class would be unnecessary.

root_cause: analyze_param() in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py branches on the annotation type first. If the annotation is a special injected type (Request, WebSocket, HTTPConnection, Response, StarletteBackgroundTasks, SecurityScopes), it runs `assert depends is None, "Cannot specify `Depends` for type ..."`. So `Annotated[Response, Depends(f)]` and `response: Response = Depends(f)` raise an AssertionError when the route is defined, even though the explicit Depends should win. This regressed when Annotated support landed in 0.95.0.
best_solution: In analyze_param, guard the special-type branch with `depends is None and lenient_issubclass(type_annotation, (Request, WebSocket, HTTPConnection, Response, StarletteBackgroundTasks, SecurityScopes))` and delete the `assert depends is None` line inside it. With an explicit Depends, control falls through to the normal dependency path: the dependency is called, and its return value is injected (it can be the injected Response, or a new JSONResponse the endpoint then returns). With no Depends, the old special injection still happens. The field_info assert stays, so `Annotated[Response, Query()]` is still rejected. The statement says exactly this: 'check for Depends before applying special type handling'.
acceptable_alternatives: Any reordering that puts the `depends is not None` check ahead of the special-type check, e.g. an early `if depends is not None: <dependency path>` before the lenient_issubclass block. Keeping the assert and only special-casing Response would fail the BackgroundTasks test (test_background_tasks_with_depends_annotated).

locating_signals: The statement names the function (`analyze_param()`), quotes the exact assertion text ('Cannot specify `Depends` for type Response'), and describes the fix ('check for Depends before applying special type handling'). root_cause: Upstream Starlette (Kludex/starlette PR #3117, 'Drop main deprecation warnings around applications/routing') removes the deprecated on_startup/on_shutdown constructor args, Router.startup()/shutdown(), add_event_handler(), the internal _DefaultLifespan, and the automatic wrapping of plain (async) generator lifespan functions. FastAPI's APIRouter.__init__ forwards on_startup/on_shutdown/lifespan straight to starlette.routing.Router.__init__, and APIRouter.on_event() calls the inherited self.add_event_handler(). None of this lives in the FastAPI repo, so on_event, FastAPI(on_startup=...), and generator lifespans would all break on the next Starlette release.
best_solution: Re-implement the removed Starlette machinery inside fastapi/routing.py and stop forwarding it to the base class. (1) In APIRouter.__init__, set self.on_startup = list(on_startup or []) and self.on_shutdown = list(on_shutdown or []). (2) Work out lifespan_context yourself: None -> a local _DefaultLifespan(self) whose __aenter__ awaits router._startup() and __aexit__ awaits router._shutdown(), and whose __call__(app) returns self; an async generator function -> contextlib.asynccontextmanager(lifespan); a sync generator function -> a vendored _wrap_gen_lifespan_context (contextlib.contextmanager wrapped in an _AsyncLiftContextManager that turns __enter__/__exit__ into async methods); anything else is passed through unchanged. Set self.lifespan_context and call super().__init__(routes=..., redirect_slashes=..., default=..., lifespan=lifespan_context), with no on_startup/on_shutdown. (3) Add APIRouter._startup/_shutdown, which loop over the handler lists and await a handler if is_async_callable(handler), otherwise call it. (4) Add APIRouter.add_event_handler(event_type, func): assert the type is 'startup' or 'shutdown' and append to the matching list. The existing on_event decorator keeps calling self.add_event_handler, so it now resolves to FastAPI's version. The code is vendored rather than imported so it doesn't depend on Starlette private symbols. The reasoning chain from the statement: find every place FastAPI leans on the Starlette lifecycle API (inherited methods and constructor kwargs), read the base-class source in site-packages, and copy the behavior across.
acceptable_alternatives: Any implementation that keeps on_startup/on_shutdown/add_event_handler/on_event working without passing them to Starlette, and that turns sync and async generator lifespans into async context managers before calling super().__init__. Importing starlette.routing._wrap_gen_lifespan_context / _DefaultLifespan would pass the tests in an env with the old Starlette, but it defeats the point, because those symbols are what is being removed. The v7-style patch (drop the kwargs from super().__init__ and append to self.on_startup in on_event) passes in the Kaggle env only because the installed Starlette (0.52.1 pinned in the env files) still initializes self.on_startup and still runs the handlers through its own _DefaultLifespan.
hidden_test_demands: 3 new tests appended to tests/test_router_events.py (9 tests collected in total): test_router_async_shutdown_handler (an async @app.on_event('shutdown') handler must be awaited on TestClient exit, so state.app_shutdown flips False->True); test_router_sync_generator_lifespan (FastAPI(lifespan=<plain def with yield>) must run the startup part on entry and the shutdown part on exit); test_router_async_generator_lifespan (same with an async def generator that has not been wrapped in asynccontextmanager). The existing tests (router/app on_event startup+shutdown, nested lifespan state) must keep passing. No new public API name is checked. The harness uses its own pytest.ini, so Starlette's generator-lifespan DeprecationWarnings do not turn into errors the way FastAPI's own filterwarnings=error config would.
locating_signals: The statement names `on_event` and 'the next Starlette' but no file or function. `git grep on_event` leads to APIRouter.on_event in fastapi/routing.py (~line 4480), which calls self.add_event_handler. That method is NOT defined anywhere in the repo: it is inherited from starlette.routing.Router in site-packages. APIRouter.__init__ (~line 900) forwards on_startup/on_shutdown/lifespan to super().__init__. The key step is to read the installed base class (python -c 'import inspect, starlette.routing as r; print(inspect.getsource(r.Router))') and see what 'the next Starlette' drops.
our_outcome_summary: Only v7 passed (kaggle_env_pass v4=false, v6=false, v7=true, v8=false). v4 (81 s, 86 calls), v6 (460 s, 57 calls) and v8 (94 s, 75 calls) produced empty patches: each died with litellm ContextWindowExceededError (32768-token limit), and v4 and v8 burned about 1.1M prompt tokens. The traces show the same loop every time: the agent ran `git grep -n "def add_event_handler"` or `grep -r` on it 10-20 times, found nothing (the method lives in Starlette's site-packages, not the repo), then paged through 50-300-line windows of the 4,500-line routing.py and applications.py until the context overflowed. It never inspected starlette.routing. v7 (169 s, 102 calls, 2186 chars) passed with a shallow patch: it removed on_startup/on_shutdown from the super().__init__ call and made on_event append straight to self.on_startup/self.on_shutdown, falling back to self.add_event_handler for other event types. It passed only because the env's old Starlette still sets self.on_startup = [] and runs the handlers through its own _DefaultLifespan, and still wraps generator lifespans. In substance the patch is wrong. FastAPI(on_startup=[...]) and router add_event_handler are now silently dropped (the kwargs are no longer forwarded or stored), the `if self.on_startup is None` guards are dead code, and nothing works on the next Starlette. It also added tests/test_on_event_reimpl.py, which collected 0 items.
generalizable_lesson: When the code calls a method on self (or passes kwargs to super().__init__) and grep finds no definition in the repo, the method is inherited from a third-party base class. Stop re-grepping and read the installed source: `python -c "import inspect, pkg.mod as m; print(inspect.getsource(m.Base.method))"` or `python -c "import pkg; print(pkg.__file__)"` plus a targeted sed. A statement like 'compatible with the next version of <dependency>' means: list every inherited method, constructor kwarg and implicit behavior the repo relies on, then vendor it locally (store the state on self, implement the methods, stop forwarding the removed kwargs). Keep existing public entry points working, both constructor args and decorators. On huge files, never page through large windows. Grep for line numbers and read 20-40 lines around each hit, and treat the same failing grep returning nothing twice as a signal to change strategy.

root_cause: PR #14851 re-implemented on_startup/on_shutdown inside FastAPI because newer Starlette dropped them. APIRouter.__init__ assigned self.on_startup / self.on_shutdown from its arguments BEFORE calling super().__init__() (starlette.routing.Router.__init__), and the Starlette parent also assigns self.on_startup/self.on_shutdown (to its own, empty, arguments), so the parent constructor clobbered the user-supplied handlers. FastAPI(on_startup=[...]) and APIRouter(on_startup=[...]) handlers were silently never run.
best_solution: In APIRouter.__init__, move the block that sets self.on_startup = [] if on_startup is None else list(on_startup) (and the same for on_shutdown) from before super().__init__(...) to after it (gold puts it right after the prefix asserts, before self.prefix = prefix). The lifespan default (_DefaultLifespan reading self.on_startup at run time) is unchanged, so once the attributes survive construction the handlers run on TestClient/uvicorn startup and shutdown, including handlers from included routers and sub-routers. The statement states the cause outright: 'set before calling super().__init__ and is overridden by router.__init__'.
acceptable_alternatives: Any placement of the two assignments after super().__init__() works (all our agents put it immediately after super().__init__, before the prefix asserts). Passing the handlers through to the parent is not an option because the target Starlette version no longer accepts on_startup/on_shutdown.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_router_events.py::test_startup_shutdown_handlers_as_parameters: FastAPI(on_startup=[...], on_shutdown=[...]), APIRouter(on_startup/on_shutdown) and a nested sub-router included via include_router; asserts all six flags are False before TestClient, the three startup flags True inside `with TestClient(app)` (shutdown still False), GET / returns 200 {'message': 'Hello World'}, and all six True after exit. No new API names or strings.
locating_signals: The statement names APIRouter.on_startup, APIRouter.__init__, super().__init__, and links the Starlette Router.__init__ lines that overwrite the attributes. grep 'self.on_startup' in fastapi/routing.py lands on the exact block. The function is named, and the fix is fully described in words.
our_outcome_summary: Passed in the Kaggle env on all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8). Pod runs took 69/87/89/110 s with 35/24/21/42 tool calls. v4, v6 and v7 moved the identical block to directly after super().__init__(), functionally the same as gold. v8 made the same source edit but also committed a stray tests/test_reproduce_issue.py that uses the removed httpx AsyncClient(app=...) API and would not trigger lifespan anyway. It did not affect grading, but it is patch noise that could break a suite that collects every test file.
generalizable_lesson: When a subclass sets attributes and then calls super().__init__(), check whether the parent constructor assigns the same attribute names. If it does, the parent silently overwrites them, so do the subclass assignments after the super() call. Watch for this in any 'X parameter is ignored / has no effect' bug. Also: take out scratch reproduction test files before finishing. Only edit tests when the task asks for it.
one_line_solution: Move the on_startup/on_shutdown assignments to after super().__init__() in APIRouter.__init__.

root_cause: Two issues. (1) In FastAPI.setup(), the /openapi.json handler ran self.servers.insert(0, {'url': root_path}) on every request whose root_path was new. self.servers is the list the user passed in (servers or []), and self.openapi() caches a schema that holds that same list. So one request's root_path stayed in the servers list for every later request, root paths from different requests piled up, and the user's configured servers list was changed in place. (2) get_swagger_ui_html embedded json.dumps(...) of swagger_ui_parameters and init_oauth inside a <script> tag without escaping, so a value containing '</script>' could close the tag.
best_solution: applications.py: never write to self.servers. In the handler, get schema = self.openapi(), which stays cached and unchanged. If root_path and self.root_path_in_servers are both set and root_path is not already a server URL in the schema, build a copy for this response only: schema = dict(schema); schema['servers'] = [{'url': root_path}] + schema.get('servers', []). Return that copy. The root_path still shows up in that response (the feature keeps working) but nothing is stored. docs.py: add a helper _html_safe_json(v) = json.dumps(v).replace('<','\\u003c').replace('>','\\u003e').replace('&','\\u0026'). Use it for both the key and the value of every swagger_ui_parameters entry and for the ui.initOAuth(...) argument. The default json.dumps separators stay as they are, so the output still contains '"clientId": "my-client"'. The key reading is that 'do not store root_path in servers' means don't keep it between requests, not don't include it. 'Escape Swagger UI configs' covers every JSON blob in the template, both the parameters loop and initOAuth.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_openapi_cache_root_path.py: test_root_path_does_not_persist_across_requests (a TestClient with root_path='/evil-api' MUST see '/evil-api' in servers, and a later client with no root_path must not), test_multiple_different_root_paths_do_not_accumulate, test_legitimate_root_path_still_appears (root_path='/api/v1' -> '/api/v1' in servers), test_configured_servers_not_mutated (the list passed as servers= is unchanged after a request). tests/test_swagger_ui_escape.py: test_init_oauth_html_chars_are_escaped (the body has no '
locating_signals: The statement names root_path, servers, and Swagger UI configs, but no files or functions. grep root_path_in_servers / servers.insert leads to FastAPI.setup() in fastapi/applications.py. grep 'Swagger UI' / json.dumps leads to get_swagger_ui_html in fastapi/openapi/docs.py. All four configs found both files. Location was not the problem. The problem was how they read the statement and whether they covered every call site.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed in the Kaggle env. v4, v6 and v7 all took 'do not store root_path in servers' to mean delete the root_path insertion entirely. That breaks the documented root_path_in_servers feature, so test_root_path_does_not_persist_across_requests and test_legitimate_root_path_still_appears fail ('/api/v1' in [] -> False). v4 escaped < and > in both swagger_ui_parameters and init_oauth, which passes all 3 swagger tests, so it went 5/7. v6 escaped only the parameter values and missed initOAuth (3 failed). v7 escaped only initOAuth and missed the parameters (3 failed). v8 set the root_path_in_servers default to False and left the handler alone. It then json.dumps-quoted openapi_url and oauth2_redirect_url instead of escaping the config JSON, so 4 of 7 failed. Pod runs: 86-133 s, 27-61 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says 'do not store X' or 'do not persist X', fix the state that leaks: build the value fresh or copy it for each request, and don't change shared or cached objects or lists the caller passed in. Do not delete the feature that produces X. Before removing any behavior, grep for its flag (here root_path_in_servers) and run the existing tests that use it. If they break, you misread the request. When asked to 'escape' something, find every place the same unsafe pattern occurs in that function (grep json.dumps inside HTML/script templates) and route them all through one helper, instead of patching the first call site you see. Keep the serializer's default output format (separators, spacing) so strings that existing tests check stay the same.
acceptable_alternatives: Any handler that returns a per-request copy with root_path prepended to servers and never changes self.servers or the cached openapi_schema (for example copy.deepcopy(self.openapi()), or building servers = [{'url': root_path}, *self.servers] inside a fresh dict). Escaping only < and > (without &) is enough for the hidden tests, as long as it covers both the swagger_ui_parameters loop and init_oauth. Using json.dumps(..., separators=(',', ':')) would fail test_normal_init_oauth_still_works.
one_line_solution: Never mutate self.servers: add root_path per response on a copy of the cached schema; escape swagger params and initOAuth JSON through one helper.

root_cause: Only the Pydantic-model header path is affected. Scalar Header() params already get a hyphenated alias in analyze_param, so they reject underscore headers. For `data: Model = Header()`, request_params_to_args looks each model field up under the hyphenated alias ('x-user-id') but only adds that alias to processed_keys. The next loop copies every unprocessed received key into params_to_process as an 'extra', so an 'x_user_id' header is copied under the field's own name. That means an underscore-only header validates (200 instead of 422), and when both headers are sent the underscore value overwrites the hyphenated one.
best_solution: In request_params_to_args, after `processed_keys.add(alias or get_validation_alias(field))`, also call `processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))`. The field's unconverted name (e.g. 'x_user_id') then counts as consumed and is never copied back in as an extra key. Hyphenated headers still map to the field, underscore-only headers fail with loc ['header','x_user_id'], and extra='allow' models still receive unrelated extra headers.
