root_cause: New feature, not a bug. FastAPI had no built-in way to serve a static SPA build (dist/) at low priority. A plain Mount/StaticFiles is matched in route order, so it can shadow API routes, 405 partial matches and slash redirects. It also has no SPA fallback (index.html for navigation, 404.html for missing assets), and it does not follow include_router prefixes the way FastAPI's lazily built _IncludedRouter tree does.
best_solution: Add frontend(path, *, directory, fallback='auto'|'index.html'|'404.html'|None, check_dir=True) to APIRouter, and have FastAPI.frontend delegate to self.router.frontend. The router keeps a separate _low_priority_routes list holding one _FrontendRouteGroup (stored as _frontend_routes). The group holds _FrontendRoute objects whose .app is a _FrontendStaticFiles, a StaticFiles subclass with html=True and follow_symlink=False. APIRouter.app is overridden: normal routes are tried first (FULL, then the first PARTIAL, then redirect_slashes), and only then _match_low_priority. That method walks the router's own low-priority routes plus each _IncludedRouter's effective_low_priority_routes(), which is cached by routes_version and applies the include prefix through with_prefix. When several frontends match, the longest prefix wins, matching on segment boundaries. The frontend path comes from a fastapi scope key. Behavior: GET/HEAD only (405 otherwise); a directory index redirects to add a trailing slash; the fallback 'auto' prefers 404.html (served with status 404) and otherwise serves index.html (status 200), but only for navigation requests (no file extension on the last segment, and an Accept header that allows text/html or */* without q=0). lookup errors map PermissionError to 401 and ValueError/ENAMETOOLONG to 404. check_dir raises RuntimeError('...does not exist...') for a missing directory or a missing explicit fallback file. An invalid fallback raises AssertionError mentioning 'fallback'. Frontend routes never appear in OpenAPI, and url_path_for raises NoMatchFound. docs_src/frontend/tutorial001-006_py310.py are also added, and the hidden tests run them with runpy.
acceptable_alternatives: Any design that keeps frontend matching strictly after all normal routes (including partial matches and slash redirects) and across include_router prefixes could pass the behavioral tests. However, about 10 tests reach into private internals (app.router._frontend_routes.routes[0].app.lookup_path, route_group.with_prefix/handle/url_path_for, router._low_priority_routes plus _mark_routes_changed, and an included route exposing effective_low_priority_routes() that returns the same cached list object), and 6 parametrized tests need the docs_src/frontend/tutorial00N_py310.py files. So in practice only a near-copy of the gold structure passes everything.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_frontend.py, 60 test cases (47 functions, some parametrized). Public API: app.frontend(path, directory=Path|str, fallback=..., check_dir=...) and router.frontend(...) honoring the APIRouter prefix plus nested include_router prefixes, and root_path. Exact behaviors checked: an API route wins over a frontend file; a POST to an API path returns 405, not the frontend; the fallback 'auto' prefers 404.html (status 404) over index.html (status 200); the index fallback only fires for Accept text/html, xhtml or */*, respects q=0, and ignores an invalid q value; asset-like paths get no index fallback; fallback=None gives the JSON body {"detail":"Not Found"}; a directory redirects to a trailing slash; path traversal (including %5c) and symlinks cannot escape; websocket routes win; HEAD works; other methods return 405; RuntimeError match 'does not exist', 'index.html' or '404.html' when check_dir is on; AssertionError match 'fallback' for an invalid value; nothing appears in openapi. root_cause: HTTPAdapter.request_url returns request.path_url verbatim. For http://127.0.0.1:10000//v:h that is '//v:h'. urllib3's ConnectionPool.urlopen calls parse_url on it, reads the leading '//' as a network-path reference (authority 'v:h'), fails the host:port regex and raises LocationParseError: Failed to parse: //v:h.
best_solution: In HTTPAdapter.request_url (src/requests/adapters.py), right after `url = request.path_url`, add `if url.startswith('//'): url = f"/{url.lstrip('/')}"`. This collapses runs of leading slashes into one slash only in the request-uri passed to conn.urlopen, so urllib3 no longer parses it as an authority. PreparedRequest.url stays as written, and the proxied branch (urldefragauth of the full URL) is unaffected. The statement points here: 'request-uri' plus 'ConnectionPool.urlopen' lead to the adapter method that builds the string handed to urlopen.
acceptable_alternatives: Normalizing the path in PreparedRequest.prepare_url (models.py) also passes the hidden test, because path_url then comes out as '/v:h'. All four of our configs did this. It changes wider behavior, though: it rewrites the user-visible PreparedRequest.url and Response.url for every adapter, including proxied requests, where the gold fix touches only the on-the-wire request-uri.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_adapters.py::test_request_url_trims_leading_path_separators. It builds HTTPAdapter(), prepares Request('GET', 'http://127.0.0.1:10000//v:h') and asserts a.request_url(p, {}) == '/v:h'. No exact message strings and no new API, only the return value of the existing request_url.
locating_signals: The terms 'request-uri', 'ConnectionPool.urlopen' and 'leading / (path-separator)s' point to HTTPAdapter.request_url, the method whose return value is passed to conn.urlopen. The function is not named in the statement. The linked issue's traceback runs adapters.send -> conn.urlopen -> parse_url. The agents followed 'path' to models.prepare_url instead, which also works for the test.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) passed in the Kaggle env. Pod runs took 48-73 s and 24-42 calls, with patches of about 500 chars. None edited the gold location. All four patched PreparedRequest.prepare_url in src/requests/models.py to collapse leading '//' in the path (v4 did it right after parse_url; v6 rewrote the bare-domain branch as `'/' + path.lstrip('/') if path else '/'`; v7 and v8 added an elif after the empty-path check). The test passes because request_url reads path_url, which is derived from the normalized url. The semantics are broader than the gold fix: the user-visible prepared URL changes, and the change covers proxied requests too.
generalizable_lesson: When a hidden test is likely to call the function that produces the value that crashes downstream, fix it at the last point before the hand-off to the third-party library. The statement names the consumer ('bypasses that logic in ConnectionPool.urlopen'), so grep for calls to that consumer and patch the argument there. Normalizing further upstream can pass this kind of test, but it also changes user-visible state, and a test that checks the upstream object unchanged would fail. Prefer the narrowest fix that sits closest to the consumer.
one_line_solution: In HTTPAdapter.request_url collapse a leading '//' in path_url to '/' before urlopen.

root_cause: In Table._render the box_segments list was built in the order [head, foot, mid], but it is consumed as `box_segments[0 if first else (2 if last else 1)]`, i.e. index 1 = middle rows and index 2 = last row. So middle body rows got the foot_left/foot_vertical/foot_right characters and the last row got the mid_* characters. Invisible with stock boxes, where mid and foot glyphs are usually identical.
best_solution: Swap the second and third tuples in the box_segments list in rich/table.py::Table._render so the order is (head_*), (mid_*), (foot_*), matching the index expression `0 if first else (2 if last else 1)`. Reasoning from the statement: it says mid glyphs show on the last line and foot glyphs show mid-body, which means the two are swapped. Grep for `foot_left` / `mid_left` in table.py to find the one list literal, then check it against the index expression. Leave the indexing alone: the first row always uses head_* and the last row always uses foot_*, even when show_header/show_footer are False, and the hidden test expects exactly that.

The first rendered row uses 1/2/3 and the last uses 7/8/9 even when there is no header or footer; middle rows use 4/5/6. Only the list reorder is needed.
locating_signals: The statement names the Box attributes (head_left, mid_left, foot_left, ...) and says 'table rendering order'. Grepping `foot_left` in rich/table.py finds the single box_segments literal in Table._render. The function is not named, but the file and attributes are unambiguous.

root_cause: rich.repr.auto's generated __rich_repr__ (auto_rich_repr in rich/repr.py) decided whether an __init__ parameter has a default with `param.default == param.empty`. When the default is an object with a custom __eq__ that returns True against inspect.Parameter.empty, the parameter was treated as having no default. Its value was then yielded positionally instead of as `name=value`.
best_solution: Use an identity check for the sentinel: `if param.default is param.empty:`. inspect.Parameter.empty is a singleton sentinel class, so `is` is the right test and never calls user-defined __eq__. After the change the StupidClass default takes the else branch and yields (name, value, default), so the repr shows `another=<StupidClass ...>`. It is a one-line change. The statement says the check is `== Parameters.empty`, and grepping for `== param.empty` finds the only site.
acceptable_alternatives: Any identity-based sentinel test, e.g. `param.default is inspect.Parameter.empty` or `param.default is inspect._empty`. Wrapping __eq__ in a try/except is not enough, because the bad __eq__ returns True without raising.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_repr.py::test_rich_repr_auto adds @rich.repr.auto class Bird(name, eats, fly=True, another=StupidClass(2), extinct=NotStupid()), where StupidClass.__eq__ returns True when other is Parameter.empty. It asserts repr(Bird('penguin', ['fish'], another=stupid_class, extinct=not_stupid)) == f"Bird('penguin', ['fish'], another={repr(stupid_class)}, extinct={repr(not_stupid)})". So `another` must be rendered as a keyword and not positionally. The existing Foo/Egg repr tests must still pass.
locating_signals: The statement quotes the buggy expression `== Parameters.empty` and says the bug is in repr of classes with overridden __eq__. That leads to rich/repr.py (the rich.repr.auto decorator, inner auto_rich_repr). The linked issue #2875 gives the exact diff. The function is not named in the PR text, but grepping for `param.empty` finds the single line.
our_outcome_summary: Resolved by all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8 all kaggle_env_pass=true). Each made the identical one-line gold change `==` -> `is`. v4 and v6 also added their own test files (tests/test_custom_repr_issue.py, tests/test_issue_2875.py). v8 left a stray reproduce_issue.py at the repo root. v7 was the cleanest, with only the source change. None of the extra files broke the hidden tests. Pod runs: 40-73 s, 24-27 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When code compares a value that may come from users (defaults, config values, arbitrary objects) against a sentinel such as inspect.Parameter.empty, None, a MISSING/_UNSET object, or dataclasses.MISSING, use `is`/`is not` and never `==`, because user __eq__ can return anything. If a statement quotes a buggy expression, grep for it and make the minimal change at that exact spot. Leave extra repro scripts out of the final patch.

root_cause: PromptBase.check_choice did an exact `value.strip() in self.choices` membership test, so there was no way to accept 'paul' for choice 'Paul'. New feature: an opt-in case_sensitive flag.

In process_response, after the choice passes validation and case_sensitive is False, return the canonical choice rather than what the user typed: `self.response_type(self.choices[[c.lower() for c in self.choices].index(value.lower())])`. root_cause: Text.expand_tabs rebuilt the text by appending the padding spaces as a separate string styled with the Text's base style (self.style), so the padding lost any span styles that covered the tab. It also computed tab stops from character length (len) rather than cell width, so wide characters (emoji) produced the wrong number of spaces. In addition, Text.append / append_text / append_tokens created spans for empty-string styles ('' is not None), which left spurious Span(x, y, '') entries in the result.
best_solution: Add Span.extend(cells) (returns a Span with end+cells, or self if cells==0) and Text.extend_style(spaces) (no-op for spaces<=0; otherwise append spaces and extend every span whose end >= len(self), or just extend plain if no spans). Rewrite expand_tabs: for each line from split('\n', include_separator=True), pass lines without tabs through unchanged; otherwise split on '\t' with include_separator, replace the trailing tab of each part with one space, track cell_position += part.cell_len, and if cell_position % tab_size is nonzero call part.extend_style(tab_size - remainder); collect parts and Text('').join them, then copy plain/spans back into self. Change 'if style is not None' to 'if style' in append, append_text and append_tokens so empty styles add no spans. Also Text.tab_size default becomes None and __rich_console__ uses console.tab_size when self.tab_size is None. The reasoning: the style of the tab is exactly the set of spans ending at the tab's end, so extending those spans over the inserted spaces carries the style; tab stops are defined in terminal cells, not characters.
acceptable_alternatives: Any expand_tabs that (a) uses cell_len for tab stops, (b) extends every span covering the tab over the padding (producing exactly the per-part spans the tests list, e.g. Span(0,4,'bold'), Span(4,7,'bold') rather than one merged span), (c) emits no empty-style spans, and (d) exposes Text.extend_style(spaces) with the exact semantics above. The exact span list is asserted, so structurally different but visually equivalent span sets fail.

It does not mention cell width, empty-style spans, the Text.extend_style or Span.extend helpers, or the Panel rendering change; those come only from the hidden tests.

root_cause: rich.markup.escape() only doubled backslashes that immediately precede a tag-like '[...]' match. A value ending in a lone backslash (e.g. 'C:\\' i.e. C:\) was returned unchanged, so when interpolated as f"[red]{escape(value)}[/red]" the trailing backslash escaped the following closing tag and printed 'C:[/red]'.
best_solution: Fix it in escape() (the function the issue says fails), not in render(). After the existing regex substitution, if the result ends with a single backslash (endswith('\\') and not endswith('\\\\')), append one more backslash so the escaped string ends in an escaped backslash; render() then turns '\\\\[' back into a literal backslash followed by a real tag. This works because escape's contract is 'safe to embed next to any markup', and the only place a trailing backslash hurts is the boundary with the next tag the caller appends.
acceptable_alternatives: Any escape()-side change that doubles an odd run of trailing backslashes (the issue's own regex (?<![\\])(?:[\\][\\])*[\\]$) passes. v4 also made the tag regex lazy ((\\*?)) which was harmless here. Changing render() instead is NOT acceptable: it alters how existing escaped markup renders and breaks test_render_escape.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_markup.py::test_escape_backslash_end: escape('C:\\') == 'C:\\\\' (Python literals: C:\ becomes C:\\); f'[red]{escape(value)}[/red]' == '[red]C:\\\\[/red]'; Text.from_markup(...).plain == 'C:\\' and spans == [Span(0, 3, 'red')]. Existing test_render_escape must keep passing (render semantics unchanged).
locating_signals: Title 'Fix escaping trailing backslash' plus linked issue #2987 titled 'Escape vs trailing backslash' naming rich.markup.escape and giving a repro and a candidate regex. The statement itself only has the title and URL, so the function name comes from the word 'escaping' and the issue text; rich/markup.py:escape is the only escape function in the markup module.

root_cause: The ANSI tokenizer regex re_ansi in rich/ansi.py only matched OSC (ESC ]...ESC \), the single-char escapes in [(@-Z\-_] and CSI (ESC [ ...). Fp private escapes ESC 0 to ESC ? (0x30-0x3F, e.g. ESC 7/ESC 8 cursor save/restore used by Alpine apk) were not matched, so Text.from_ansi kept them as plain text and they ended up in output (test shows '?x' instead of 'x').
best_solution: Add one alternative at the front of the verbose regex: `(?:\x1b[0-?])|`. It is non-capturing, so match.groups() is (None, None) and _ansi_tokenize takes the else branch, yielding an empty token: the sequence is consumed and emits nothing. It does not overlap the other alternatives because '[' (0x5B) and ']' (0x5D) are outside 0x30-0x3F. The existing class [(@-Z\-_] must stay unchanged, because the tokenizer has a special case `if sgr == "(": position = end + 1` that strips charset designators such as ESC ( B. An equally valid fix is to extend the class to [(0-?@-Z\-_]: sgr='0'..'?' is truthy, not '(', and does not end in 'm', so it is skipped too.
acceptable_alternatives: Extend the capturing class to [(0-?@-Z\-_], keeping the leading '('. Anything that deletes '(' from the class breaks test_decode_issue_2688.

The existing test_decode_issue_2688 cases (ESC ( B, ESC ( J charset escapes stripped) must still pass.
locating_signals: The statement says 'updates the ANSI parser' and gives the exact byte range \x1b0-\x1b?. grep for 'ansi' leads to rich/ansi.py, where the module-level re_ansi regex is the only parser. No function is named, but the file holds only one regex, so there is nowhere else to put the fix.

root_cause: Console._check_buffer wrote and flushed self.file with no BrokenPipeError handling. When stdout is piped to a reader that exits early (`python -m rich | head -1`), the write/flush raised a traceback. Catching the error is not enough: the unflushed data left in sys.stdout makes the interpreter's shutdown flush fail again ('Exception ignored ... BrokenPipeError'), so the process exits with code 120.
best_solution: Split _check_buffer so that the write/flush body moves to a new _write_buffer(), and wrap the call as `try: self._write_buffer() except BrokenPipeError: self.on_broken_pipe()`. The new public hook Console.on_broken_pipe() follows the CPython 'note on SIGPIPE' recipe: set self.quiet = True, `devnull = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY); os.dup2(devnull, sys.stdout.fileno())`, then `raise SystemExit(1)`. Pointing fd 1 at devnull stops the interpreter's shutdown flush from failing again, which would otherwise exit 120, and exit code 1 matches Python's normal EPIPE convention. Because the whole write path sits inside one try, both write() and flush() are covered. The other two hunks only reformat conditional expressions (black).
acceptable_alternatives: Any handler around the whole write+flush path that redirects stdout's fd to os.devnull (or otherwise stops the shutdown flush from raising) and then exits with SystemExit(1). Catching the error and returning, or exiting with 0, fails.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_console.py::test_brokenpipeerror (skipped on win32) runs `python -m rich | head -1` through subprocess.Popen and asserts proc1.returncode == 1 and head returncode == 0. So the process must exit with exactly 1: no traceback that leaves the exit code at 1 by accident, no 0, and no 120 from a failed shutdown flush of sys.stdout.
locating_signals: The statement is the terse PR body 'handle broken pipe / Handle BrokenPipe exceptions / Fixes issue 1591'. It does not name a function. The issue traceback (not in the statement) points at console.py _exit_buffer -> _check_buffer -> self.file.write. The fix recipe (dup2 devnull + sys.exit(1)) appears only in an issue comment by lmmx, which cites the Python signal docs 'note on SIGPIPE'. Grepping for self.file.write/flush in console.py finds the location.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8) failed in the Kaggle env, each in 57-188s and 25-102 calls. Every config found the right spot (_check_buffer) and 97 other tests passed. The exit semantics were wrong each time. v4 and v8 (identical patches) added `except BrokenPipeError: return` around write() only. The later self.file.flush() still raised, and the exit code was 120. v6 raised SystemExit(0) and got 120, because the shutdown flush of sys.stdout failed again. v7 also wrapped flush() with return, but data left in the buffer still failed at interpreter shutdown, giving 120. None of them redirected fd 1 to devnull, and none exited with 1.
generalizable_lesson: When handling BrokenPipeError or SIGPIPE in CLI output code, use the CPython recipe: catch around the whole write+flush path, `os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())`, then `sys.exit(1)`. Swallowing the error, or exiting with 0, leaves a buffered stdout that fails again at interpreter shutdown and exits with 120. More generally, when a statement is only 'Fixes <issue URL>', the linked issue's comments often hold the expected recipe and exit code. Verify the fix end to end with a real pipe (`python -m pkg | head -1; echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}`), not only by reading the code.
one_line_solution: Catch BrokenPipeError around write+flush, dup2 devnull onto stdout and exit(1) (CPython SIGPIPE recipe) via a Console.on_broken_pipe hook.

The forward-only loop cannot step back, so it returns a left part one or more cells too wide (e.g. 24 cells for cut=23).
best_solution: Keep the proportional guess but make the search two-way. Loop: before=text[:pos], out_by=cell_len(before)-cut. If out_by==0, split at pos. If out_by==-1 and text[pos] is double-width, the cut lands inside that character: return (text[:pos]+' ', ' '+text[pos+1:]). If out_by==+1 and text[pos-1] is double-width, return (text[:pos-1]+' ', ' '+text[pos:]). Otherwise pos += 1 if cell_pos < cut, else pos -= 1. This drops the 'will never reach here' assertion. Invariant: cell_len(left)==cut and cell_len(right)==cell_length-cut for every cut from 0 to cell_length. A plain linear scan from pos=0 is also correct, just O(n).
acceptable_alternatives: Start the scan at pos=0 (or walk back until cell_len(text[:pos]) <= cut before scanning forward). The v6 patch did this (pos=0, before='', cell_pos=0) and passed. Any split that keeps cell_len(left)==cut, pads a double-width char cut in half with one space on each side, and leaves the other split tests (emoji, doubles) green works.

For every position in range(0, cell_length+1) it asserts cell_len(left.text)==position and cell_len(right.text)==cell_length-position. Existing test_split_cells_emoji and test_split_cells_doubles must still pass, so a double-width char cut in half becomes ' ' on both sides.

The existing test_split_cells_mixed test (and its comment citing textual#4996) points at the same code.

root_cause: The fast-path character class in rich/cells.py `_is_single_cell_widths = re.compile("^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$")` had two typos: the ASCII range stopped at U+006F ('o') instead of U+007E ('~'), so 'p'..'~' fell off the fast path, and `\u00a0\u02ff` was missing its hyphen, so it matched only those two code points instead of the Latin-1/Latin-Extended range. Most ordinary text therefore took the slow per-character width lookup.
best_solution: Rewrite the class as `^[\u0020-\u007e\u00a0-\u02ff\u0370-\u0482\u2500-\u25FF]*$`: end printable ASCII at U+007E (not U+007F, which is DEL, a control char), restore the missing hyphen so U+00A0-U+02FF is a range, and add box drawing plus block elements (U+2500-U+25FF), the single-width glyphs rich draws all the time in tables and panels. In segment.py the PR also adds an `assert cut >= 0` guard and an Args docstring to Segment.split_cells, which callers of the fast path rely on. How to reach it from the statement: read every range in the class, check each endpoint against what 'most common single-width characters' should mean, then confirm with cell_len/get_character_cell_size that every added code point is really width 1.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_is_single_cell_widths imports the private name `_is_single_cell_widths` from rich.cells. It asserts that every string.printable character with ord >= 32 matches (so U+0070-U+007E must be included), that every character of the box-drawing string "┌─┬┐│ ││├─┼┤│ ││├─┼┤├─┼┤│ ││└─┴┘" matches (U+2500-U+257F must be in the class), and that the emoji "💩😽" and the kana "わさび" do NOT match. Latin-1 is not checked, so the missing-hyphen fix is not needed to pass.
locating_signals: The title 'Regex error' plus 'fast path for strings with single-width characters' leads straight to the only such regex, `_is_single_cell_widths` in rich/cells.py, whose comment reads 'Regex to match sequence of the most common character ranges'. The statement names the purpose, not the variable. Nothing in it mentions box drawing, which the test requires.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env. v4, v6 and v7 submitted empty patches (0 chars) after 366-500 s and 64-85 tool calls: they explored and never committed an edit. v8 (87 s, 51 calls, 465-char patch) changed only the ASCII endpoint, from \u006f to \u007f. That makes the printable checks pass but wrongly admits DEL (U+007F, a control char). It left the missing hyphen in `\u00a0\u02ff` and did not add the box-drawing range, so the hidden test failed with `AssertionError: assert None where None = _is_single_cell_widths('┌')` (tests/test_cells.py:75); 7 of the 8 tests passed.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says a regex or character class is wrong, audit every term, not just the first bad one. Look for off-by-one endpoints, missing '-' that turns a range into two single characters, and ranges that include control characters. Then check the class by brute force against the ground-truth function it shortcuts (here, the slow-path width lookup) over the population the code actually handles, including the library's own heavy-use characters (box drawing and symbols for a TUI or rendering library). A fast-path predicate should cover the common cases the codebase itself produces, and hidden tests often probe exactly those. Also, always submit your best partial edit rather than running out of turns with an empty diff.
one_line_solution: Fix _is_single_cell_widths: end ASCII at U+007E, restore the U+00A0-U+02FF range hyphen, add box drawing U+2500-U+25FF.
flip_note: Box-drawing range is a hidden choice; brute-force check vs slow path might surface it.

root_cause: Console.is_terminal (rich/console.py) had only two overrides: an explicit force_terminal, and FORCE_COLOR, where any value at all meant 'terminal'. There was no environment switch that could force TTY behaviour on or off. The semantics of the new variable are defined only in a maintainer comment on linked issue #2924: TTY_COMPATIBLE=1 means assume a TTY, TTY_COMPATIBLE=0 means assume it is not a TTY, and a blank or any other value means auto-detect. The statement is just the PR title and body ('Implement new TTY_COMPATIBLE environment variable' plus that link), so none of these semantics are visible to the agent.
best_solution: In Console.is_terminal, after the _force_terminal, IDLE and Jupyter checks and before FORCE_COLOR and isatty, read `tty_compatible = environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE', '')`. If it equals '0', return False. If it equals '1', return True. For any other value, fall through. Then FORCE_COLOR returns `force_color != ''` (the force-color.org rule) and no longer caches `self._force_terminal`, and finally the code auto-detects with `self.file.isatty()`. The PR also changed NO_COLOR to count only when non-empty (`self._environ.get('NO_COLOR', '') != ''`) and added TTY_COMPATIBLE to the diagnose.py env list. Neither change is tested. The reasoning comes from the variable's name: 'COMPATIBLE' reads as a boolean flag, so it should be tri-state (1 forces on, 0 forces off, anything else defers to auto-detect). It should not copy FORCE_COLOR's 'presence means on' rule, because under that rule TTY_COMPATIBLE=0 would turn the TTY on.
hidden_test_demands: New test tests/test_console.py::test_tty_compatible. The other test_patch hunks only add '-> None' annotations and change \x1B to \x1b. The new test uses FakeFile (isatty returns False) and FakeTTY (isatty returns True), and each records whether isatty was called. Expected results: no env var -> isatty is called and the result follows the file. TTY_COMPATIBLE='1' on FakeFile -> is_terminal is True and isatty is NOT called. TTY_COMPATIBLE='' on FakeTTY -> True and isatty IS called. 'whatever' on FakeTTY -> True and isatty IS called. '0' on FakeTTY -> False and isatty is NOT called.
locating_signals: The statement only names the env var TTY_COMPATIBLE. Grepping for the sibling 'FORCE_COLOR' or for 'isatty' leads straight to Console.is_terminal in rich/console.py. No function is named, but the location is easy to find. The semantics are what is hard: they are only in the #2924 maintainer comment and in the new test's comments ('Blank TTY_COMPATIBLE should auto-detect', 'TTY_COMPATIBLE should override file.isatty').
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed in the Kaggle env. Each ran for 46-52 s with 15-21 calls, and every patch touched only is_terminal. v4 added a separate `if self._environ.get('TTY_COMPATIBLE') is not None: return True` after the FORCE_COLOR block. v6, v7 and v8 OR'd TTY_COMPATIBLE into the FORCE_COLOR branch (`if force_color is not None or tty_compatible is not None: self._force_terminal = True; return True`). Both versions copy FORCE_COLOR's 'any value means terminal' rule. As a result '' and 'whatever' return True without calling isatty, and '0' forces a terminal instead of disabling it. The log shows the failure at test_console.py:1098 (blank TTY_COMPATIBLE: `assert console.file.called_isatty` is False), with 1 failed and 98 passed. v6-v8 would also have failed the '0' case, because they cache _force_terminal=True.
acceptable_alternatives: Any tri-state check in is_terminal that runs before the isatty auto-detect and returns immediately on '1'/'0' passes. It can go before or after the FORCE_COLOR block, because the test passes an explicit _environ that contains only TTY_COMPATIBLE. The FORCE_COLOR empty-string change, the NO_COLOR empty-string change and the diagnose.py edit are optional for the tests.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement introduces a new env var or flag by name only, and the spec is behind a link you cannot read, do not copy the 'presence means on' semantics of a sibling variable. Use the conventional tri-state: '1' forces on, '0' forces off, and empty or any other value falls through to the existing auto-detection. The explicit values must short-circuit before the detection call, because tests often assert the detector was or was not called. Check your implementation against the obvious counter-case (VAR=0 must never enable the feature) before finishing.
one_line_solution: TTY_COMPATIBLE tri-state in Console.is_terminal: '1' True, '0' False, anything else falls through to detection.

root_cause: Traceback.extract() built Stack records with only exc_type/exc_value/frames and ignored PEP 678 Exception.__notes__ (Python 3.11+ add_note), so notes were neither stored on the trace nor rendered.
best_solution: In Traceback.extract, read notes = getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None) or [] (a list of str; attribute absent before 3.11 or when no note was added). Add a dataclass field notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list) to Stack (and _SyntaxError) and pass notes=notes when constructing them. In __rich_console__, after the exc_type/exc_value line, yield one line per note: Text.assemble(('[NOTE] ', 'traceback.note'), highlighter(note)), and register a 'traceback.note' style in default_styles.py. Key reasoning: __notes__ is a list, so the stored field should mirror it as a list with an empty-list default, not a joined or str()-ed string.
acceptable_alternatives: Any storage that keeps Stack.notes equal to the list of note strings (e.g. notes: Optional[List[str]] = None filled directly from getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None)) passes; the rendering format and style name are not tested. v4 and v6 passed while annotating the field as Optional[str] because they stored the raw list unchanged.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_traceback.py::test_notes (skipped below Python 3.11): raises 1/0, calls error.add_note('Hello') and add_note('World'), builds Traceback() inside the except, and asserts traceback.trace.stacks[0].notes == ['Hello', 'World']. Requires the attribute name `notes` on Stack and a list value in insertion order; rendering is not checked.
locating_signals: The statement is just the PR title 'Notes' plus 'Add support for Exception.__notes__'. '__notes__' points at exception handling, and in rich that means rich/traceback.py (Traceback.extract builds Stack from exc_value). No function or field is named; the field name `notes` and its list type are hidden spec, inferable only from the __notes__ attribute itself.
our_outcome_summary: v4 PASS (75s, 34 calls) and v6 PASS (95s, 52 calls): both added Stack.notes = getattr(exc_value, '__notes__', None) (typed Optional[str] but holding the list) and rendered it after exc_value. v7 FAIL (161s, 89 calls): it stored notes=safe_str(notes), which turned the list into the string "['Hello', 'World']", so the assertion stacks[0].notes == ['Hello','World'] failed (log: assert "['Hello', 'World']" == ['Hello', 'World']). v8 FAIL (35s, 30 calls): empty patch, no edit submitted.
generalizable_lesson: When a feature captures an existing language or runtime attribute (here __notes__, a list[str]), store it on the new field in the same type and shape as the source, with an empty default (default_factory=list), and put any formatting in the render step. Stringifying or joining at capture time (str(), safe_str, '\n'.join) breaks any test that compares the stored field to the original value. Also: on terse PR-title statements, name the new field after the attribute you expose (__notes__ -> notes) and make sure a final non-empty diff is actually submitted.

root_cause: Traceback.extract walks the exception chain in a `while True` loop that follows `__cause__` / `__context__` with no cycle guard, and recurses into ExceptionGroup members with no visited set. `raise e from e` makes `e.__cause__ is e`, so the loop never ends (issue 3708: hang, memory grows). A group that contains itself, directly or through another group, recurses until RecursionError (issue 3682).
best_solution: In Traceback.extract: (1) add a private `_visited_exceptions: Optional[Set[BaseException]] = None` parameter and build a shared `grouped_exceptions` set from it; when expanding an exception group, skip members already in the set, add each new one, and pass the set down in the recursive extract call so a group cycle stops. (2) Guard the chain walk: follow `__cause__` only when `cause is not None and cause is not exc_value`, use `is not None` checks for `__context__`, and only walk cause/context when `grouped_exceptions` is empty. You can get there from the statement alone: 'traceback recursion' in an exception renderer means a cycle in the exception graph (cause, context, group members), not deep user recursion. So find every loop or recursive call in extract that follows those links and give it a cycle guard. A more general version keeps one `seen` set of ids across the whole chain walk.
acceptable_alternatives: Any cycle guard in extract's cause/context loop passes the hidden test, for example a `seen = set()` of id(exc_value) that breaks when an exception comes back, or a plain `cause is not exc_value` identity check (the fix issue 3708 proposes). A visited set for group recursion is needed for 3682 but is not exercised by the hidden test.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_traceback.py::test_recursive_exception: inside `except` it runs `raise e from e` (asserts `e is e.__cause__`), then calls `console.print_exception(show_locals=True)`. The call must return; there are no assertions on the output. It goes through Console.print_exception -> Traceback -> extract, not the install() excepthook.
locating_signals: The title 'Fix traceback recursion' points to rich/traceback.py. The gold function (Traceback.extract) is not named. The key details are only in the linked issues, which the agent cannot read offline: 3708 quotes the `cause = getattr(exc_value, "__cause__", None)` block in extract and proposes `cause is not exc_value`, and 3682 shows RecursionError repeating at the recursive group-extract call in extract.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8) failed. Each test log shows 22 tests passing, then a hang on test_recursive_exception until timeout. All of them read 'recursion' as Python RecursionError from deep user code, not as a cyclic exception chain. v4 (251s, 27 calls) wrapped the install() sys.excepthook in `try/except RecursionError` and added a stray reproduce_recursion.py. That was the wrong place, because the test calls console.print_exception directly, and the wrong bug, because the loop is iterative and never raises RecursionError. v6 (62s, 39 calls) produced an empty patch. v7 (261s, 37 calls) only added a repro script and changed no source. v8 (324s, 43 calls) worked in the right function, Traceback.extract, but only wrapped pretty.traverse of locals in a RecursionError catch, leaving the unguarded `__cause__` loop in place.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement is only a title plus issue links you cannot read, list every reading of the key word before coding. 'Recursion' or 'infinite loop' in code that walks linked objects (exception __cause__/__context__, parent/child pointers, nested containers, graph nodes) usually means a missing cycle guard, not deep user recursion. Grep the named module for `while True` loops that follow an attribute, and for self-recursive calls, and add an identity check or a visited-id set there. Never 'fix' it by catching RecursionError in an outer wrapper: an iterative cycle hangs without growing the stack. Write the repro as a direct library call (for example raise e from e, then print the traceback) so you are exercising the core function the hidden test will call.

The existing expression then applies it, keeping is_interactive a plain attribute and letting an explicit force_interactive argument win over the env var. Also add 'TTY_INTERACTIVE' to the env list in rich/diagnose.py (untested) and tidy the typing imports. Reasoning: the statement says it 'adds to the new TTY_COMPATIBLE', so grep TTY_COMPATIBLE, see its '0'/'1'/other tri-state, and mirror it for interactivity via the injectable self._environ.

It passed, but it silently ignores the force_interactive argument and is_dumb_terminal, and it breaks code that assigns console.is_interactive. So it passed without being a faithful fix.

locating_signals: The env var name TTY_INTERACTIVE and the phrase 'adds to the new TTY_COMPATIBLE' point to rich/console.py, where TTY_COMPATIBLE is handled in is_terminal and is_interactive is set in __init__. Read it through the object's injectable environment, since tests pass one in. Gold also stores padding unpacked via a PaddingProperty descriptor so self.padding is always a 4-tuple, and changes `if self.padding:` to `if any(self.padding)`.

That alone is enough for the hidden test; the gold descriptor and `any(self.padding)` change are refactors that the test does not need.

root_cause: Inspect._get_signature computes `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` and then uses it as a string. A class decorated with @functools.lru_cache that has __qualname__ in __slots__ exposes __qualname__ as a member_descriptor, not a str, so later string handling raises.
best_solution: In rich/_inspect.py Inspect._get_signature, keep the existing `name or getattr(obj, '__qualname__', name)` expression (a caller-supplied name still wins), then add a type guard: if qualname is not a str, try getattr(obj, '__name__', name); if that is not a str either, fall back to name. The statement spells this out: 'checking the type of __qualname__ falling back to __name__ and if that isn't a str using the already provided fallback'. The fix works because it only changes behavior when the attribute is not a string, so normal objects render exactly as before.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_inspect.py::test_qualname_in_slots: builds `@lru_cache class Klass: __slots__ = ('__qualname__',)` and asserts inspect(Klass) raises nothing. It checks no output format. The existing PASS_TO_PASS render tests (test_render, test_inspect_coroutine, test_inspect_module_with_class, test_inspect_builtin_function_only_python311, test_can_handle_special_characters_in_docstrings[*]) pin exact output, so the precedence of `name` over `obj.__qualname__` and the empty-name fallback must stay as they were.
locating_signals: The title and body name `inspect` and `__qualname__`. Grepping rich/_inspect.py for __qualname__ finds the one `qualname = name or getattr(obj, "__qualname__", name)` line in _get_signature. The function is not named in the statement, but the grep has only two hits (the other is get_object_types_mro_as_strings, which is harmless because an f-string calls str()).
our_outcome_summary: v4 and v7 passed; v6 and v8 failed. v4 and v7 both kept `name or getattr(...)` and added the gold isinstance/__name__ fallback, plus a harmless str() tweak in get_object_types_mro_as_strings. v7 also left a stray reproduce_issue.py, which was harmless. v6 replaced the `or` with `qualname = name; if not isinstance(qualname, str): ...`. Since name is usually '' (a str), the __qualname__ fallback never ran and signatures came out as 'async def ():'. That broke 7 PASS_TO_PASS tests, including test_inspect_coroutine and test_inspect_builtin_function_only_python311. v8 reversed the precedence and always preferred obj.__qualname__ over the caller's name, so attribute rows became 'def Foo.__init__' instead of 'def __init__'. generalizable_lesson: For a 'handle an unusual value' bugfix, keep the original expression unchanged and add a type guard after it that only acts on the bad case. Do not rewrite the expression into if-chains: `a or b` falls back when a is falsy (e.g. ''), which `if not isinstance(a, str)` does not reproduce, and reordering fallbacks changes precedence. Before finishing, run the module's existing tests (pytest tests/test_<module>.py) as well as the new repro; render/snapshot tests will catch an accidental change in output.
acceptable_alternatives: Any guard that only acts when getattr(obj, '__qualname__') is not a str and keeps `name or ...` precedence, e.g. `if not isinstance(qualname, str): qualname = str(getattr(obj, '__name__', '') or name)`. Also accepting Text instances (as v4 did) is fine.
one_line_solution: Keep `name or __qualname__` and add a type guard falling back to __name__ when qualname is not a str.

root_cause: rich.cells measured width one codepoint at a time from a single CELL_WIDTHS table (rich/_cell_widths.py). Multi-codepoint graphemes were summed per codepoint: a ZWJ sequence like woman+ZWJ+wrench counted 4 cells instead of 2, and a narrow base followed by VS-16 (U+FE0F), e.g. '⬇️' or '♻️', counted 1 instead of 2 (issue #3897). chop_cells and set_cell_size also split between codepoints, so wrapping or cropping could cut a grapheme in half. Codepoints above the table's last range fell through to width 1.
best_solution: Replace the single width table with per-Unicode-version tables taken from wcwidth: package rich/_unicode_data holds VERSIONS (4.1.0 to 17.0.0), _parse_version (pads '1' or '1.2' to a 3-tuple and raises ValueError on bad input), and a cached load(version='auto') that reads the UNICODE_VERSION env var, maps 'latest' or invalid input to 17.0.0, and otherwise picks the nearest lower listed version via bisect (4.1.0 for anything below it). It returns a CellTable NamedTuple (unicode_version, widths, narrow_to_wide frozenset of VS-16-widened chars). In cells.py: get_character_cell_size(ch, unicode_version) returns 0 above the table's last range. _cell_len skips the codepoint after a ZWJ and adds +1 when VS-16 follows a char in narrow_to_wide. New split_graphemes(text) returns (list of CellSpan (start, end, cells), total width): a ZWJ extends the previous span by 2 codepoints, VS-16 extends it and may widen it, and other zero-width chars attach to the previous span. New split_text(text, cell_pos) walks the spans and, when the cut lands inside a 2-cell grapheme, returns (left + ' ', ' ' + right). set_cell_size crops via _split_text, and chop_cells builds lines from grapheme spans. Reasoning from the statement: 'split strings in to sequences that produce a single glyph', and 'used in a few low-level functions' means cell_len, set_cell_size, chop_cells and a new split function all have to become grapheme-aware. 'Same way as wcwidth' means ZWJ and VS-16 rules plus versioned width data.

root_cause: Live.stop() unconditionally calls self.console.line() (when not alt_screen and console.is_terminal) to move past the live region. When the renderable produced zero lines (e.g. Live(Group(), transient=True)), there is no region to move past, so a spurious '\n' is left behind even with transient=True (issue #3796). A renderable of [""] renders 1 line, which is why that 'hack' hid the bug.
best_solution: Only emit the trailing newline if something was actually rendered. Add a LiveRender.last_render_height property returning 0 when self._shape is None else self._shape[1] (the line count of the last render), and in Live.stop() change the guard to `if not self._alt_screen and self.console.is_terminal and self._live_render.last_render_height: self.console.line()`. Reasoning from the statement: 'empty live' + issue title 'Live with empty render leaves behind a spurious newline' -> reproduce with `with Live(Group(), console=capture_console, transient=True): pass`, see output '\x1b[?25l\r\x1b[2K\n\x1b[?25h\r', locate the only unconditional newline writer in stop(), and gate it on the rendered height. (The typing import reorder in live_render.py is cosmetic.)
acceptable_alternatives: Any gate on the last rendered height at the console.line() call in Live.stop(), e.g. `shape = self._live_render._shape; if ... and shape and shape[1]: self.console.line()`. Must not change start()/__enter__ refresh behavior, or the existing test_growing_display* byte-exact tests break.

root_cause: Table._get_padding_width (used when measuring/allocating column widths) ignored pad_edge, while the render-time get_padding() in Table._render zeroes the first column's left pad and the last column's right pad when pad_edge=False. Table.grid defaults to pad_edge=False, collapse_padding=True, so with padding=(0,1) the first column was measured 1 char wider than it renders (content padded to 4 + right pad 1 = double gap between col 1 and 2) and the last column got a spurious trailing space.
best_solution: Issue #3871: Table.grid(padding=(0,1)) with three width=3 columns prints 'aaa  aaa aaa ' (double gap after column 1). Compare the width-measurement path (_get_padding_width, called by _measure_column/_calculate_column_widths) with the render path (get_padding inside _render): render applies pad_edge, measure does not. Fix _get_padding_width to mirror render: under collapse_padding drop the left pad, and if not self.pad_edge set pad_left=0 for column_index==0 and pad_right=0 for column_index==len(self.columns)-1; return pad_left+pad_right. Output becomes 'aaa aaa aaa'. The remaining hunks are blank-line cosmetics. Side effect: rich.columns.Columns (built on a grid) loses one space in its fixed-width layout, so test_columns expected output changes.

root_cause: In Console.print, when a style= argument is given, the styled branch calls Segment.apply_style(render(renderable), style) over ALL rendered segments, including the trailing '\n' segment that Text emits as its end. With soft_wrap=False the later Segment.split_and_crop_lines pass re-splits on newlines and emits an unstyled Segment.line(), which hides the bug. With soft_wrap=True the buffer is extended with new_segments directly, so the newline itself carries the background style. The output is '\x1b[34;47mtext\x1b[0m\x1b[34;47m\n\x1b[0m', and a terminal that scrolls fills the new line with the background color.

Style the text of each line but never the newline. Add a classmethod Segment.split_lines_terminator(segments) next to Segment.split_lines. It yields (line_segments, had_newline) tuples: it partitions non-control segment text on '
', yields (line, True) at each newline and a final (line, False) if anything remains. In the styled branch of Console.print, compute render_style = self.get_style(style) and new_line = Segment.line() once. For each rendered line, extend with Segment.apply_style(line, render_style), then append the unstyled new_line if had_newline. The output for soft_wrap then matches the soft_wrap=False path: the reset comes before '
'. How to get there from the statement: run the issue's repro with soft_wrap on and off, diff the ANSI output, and see that the only difference is a styled '
'. Then find the branch where the soft_wrap path skips the line re-splitting the other path does.

root_cause: In rich 14.3.0, get_character_cell_size() in rich/cells.py returns 0 for any codepoint above the last range in the unicode width table. Nerd-font glyphs live in the Supplementary Private Use Area (e.g. U+F024D), past the table's end, so they were measured as zero-width and layouts broke.
best_solution: Change the out-of-table branch in get_character_cell_size from `return 0` to `return 1`. A codepoint the width table doesn't cover (unassigned, or private-use like nerd-font icons) should default to a single cell, which is how terminals draw them. Zero width should be kept for known combining or zero-width characters. The reasoning chain: the title says 'fix fonts' and the issue says nerd-font icons render wrong after the 14.3.0 cell-width rewrite. Call cell_len('\U000f024d'), see 0, then trace it to the `codepoint > table[-1][1]` early return.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_nerd_font asserts cell_len("\U000f024d") == 1 (regression for issue #3943). Nothing else changes, and the existing cell tests must keep passing.
locating_signals: The statement is only 'fix fonts' plus an issue URL. 'fonts' misleads toward rich/_export_format.py (Fira Code font-family in SVG/HTML export), which both non-empty agent patches edited. The real signal (nerd-font glyph U+F024D measured with the wrong width after v14.3.0) is only in the linked issue text, which the agent cannot see. The gold function (get_character_cell_size / cell_len in rich/cells.py) is not named anywhere in the statement.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4, v6, v7, v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4 (100 calls) and v7 (41 calls) produced empty patches. v6 changed the HTML export template to put 'Fira Code' in the pre font-family. v8 quoted "Fira Code" in the SVG matrix CSS and edited tests/test_console.py EXPECTED_SVG to match. Both took 'fonts' to mean CSS font-family strings in _export_format.py and never touched cells.py, so test_nerd_font failed with `assert 0 == 1` for cell_len('\U000f024d').
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a vague title plus an issue link the agent can't read, don't grep the title's noun ('fonts') for a literal match. Guess the likely user-visible symptom (glyphs misaligned or measured wrong), check the most recent change to that subsystem (git log -p on its hot files), and probe edge inputs such as private-use or out-of-range codepoints, empty values and boundary values. Look closely at early-return defaults in lookup/bisect code: a 'not found' fallback of 0 or None is a common regression. Never edit existing expected-output tests to make a cosmetic change pass.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that makes codepoints outside the width table, or in the Private Use Areas (U+E000-U+F8FF, U+F0000-U+FFFFD, U+100000-U+10FFFD), return width 1 in get_character_cell_size / cell_len, while combining and zero-width characters stay 0.
one_line_solution: Return 1 (not 0) for codepoints beyond the width table in get_character_cell_size.

root_cause: Two separate regressions from the v14.3.0 rewrite of rich/cells.py. (1) Issue #3947: in _cell_len the ZWJ branch calls next(iter_characters) to skip the character after U+200D; when ZWJ is the last character (cell_len('\u200d'), '1\u200d') next() raises StopIteration, which surfaces as RuntimeError inside console.print generators. (2) Issue #3950: get_character_cell_size looks codepoints up in the new unicode width table, which has no entries for C0/C1 control characters, so chr(1)..chr(31) and 0x7F..0x9F fall through to width 1 instead of 0 (the old _cell_widths table had (1,31,-1) and (127,159,-1)).
best_solution: In rich/cells.py: (a) at the top of get_character_cell_size add `if codepoint and codepoint < 32 or 0x07F <= codepoint < 0x0A0: return 0` so control characters are zero width before the table lookup (the fast path _is_single_cell_widths only covers 0x20-0x7E, so control chars always reach this function); also tidy the binary search to `while lower_bound <= upper_bound` and return width directly. (b) In _cell_len replace the iterator + next() with an index loop: on ZWJ do `index += 1` (skip the joined character) and always `index += 1` at the end of the loop, so a trailing ZWJ just ends the loop. Semantics kept: the character after a ZWJ is not counted, so cell_len('1\u200d2') == 1 (matches wcwidth), cell_len('\u200d') == 0, cell_len('1\u200d') == 1. The statement is only a title plus two issue links, so the second bug (control characters) is only discoverable by reading issue #3950 or by probing cell_len over edge-case inputs such as chr(0..31).
acceptable_alternatives: Wrapping next(iter_characters) in try/except StopIteration (or using next(iter_characters, None)) fixes the ZWJ half equivalently. Control-char zero width could equally be implemented in _cell_len or via a table entry, as long as cell_len(chr(i)) == 0 for i in 0..30. Changing ZWJ handling to not skip the following character (counting '1\u200d2' as 2) is NOT acceptable: the hidden test pins 1.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_zwj: cell_len('')==0, cell_len('\u200d')==0, cell_len('1\u200d')==1, cell_len('1\u200d2')==1 (character after ZWJ is swallowed, not counted). tests/test_cells.py::test_non_printable: cell_len(chr(i))==0 for every i in range(31), including chr(0).
locating_signals: Title 'Fix ZWJ and edge cases' points to zero-width-joiner (U+200D) handling, which grep finds in rich/cells.py (_cell_len and split_graphemes). No function is named. The control-character bug is invisible in the statement: 'edge cases' plus the URL of issue #3950 ('cell_len doesn't account for control characters') is the only signal, so an offline agent that cannot open the issue has to infer it.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass all false). v4 (95s, 43 calls) and v7 (68s, 29 calls) wrapped next(iter_characters) in try/except StopIteration (plus a split_graphemes bounds tweak), so test_zwj passes, but neither touched control-character widths: test_non_printable fails with `assert cell_len('\x01') == 0` (got 1). v6 (40s, 17 calls) replaced next() with `pass`, which stops swallowing the joined character, so cell_len('1\u200d2') returns 2 instead of 1, and it also missed control chars (fails both tests). v8 (374s, 24 calls) only added scratch files test_zwj.py / test_zwj_fail.py at repo root and made no source change (fails both). Common cause: every agent read the statement as 'ZWJ only' and treated the linked issue numbers as opaque; none probed other edge inputs to cell_len.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is a PR title plus 'Fixes #A / Fixes #B' with several issue links, assume each link is a distinct bug and there is more than one defect to fix; if the issue text is unavailable, treat vague words like 'edge cases' as a mandate to probe the touched function with boundary inputs (empty string, the special char alone, the special char at the end, control characters chr(0..31), 0x7F-0x9F) and compare against the documented or historical behaviour (e.g. an old lookup table or a git-log predecessor). Preserve existing semantics that the fix does not need to change (here: the char after ZWJ is skipped); make the crash path safe instead of changing what gets counted. Never leave scratch test files in the repo as the only change.
one_line_solution: Zero width for C0/C1 control characters in get_character_cell_size, and make the ZWJ next() safe at end of string.

root_cause: rich 14.3.2 rewrote split_graphemes as a while-loop in which two branches never advance `index`: (1) a zero-width non-special character (e.g. ANSI ESC \x1b, which get_character_cell_size now returns 0 for) when `spans` is still empty, because the branch is `elif spans:`; (2) a VS16 (\ufe0f) when `last_measured_character` is None, because the branch is `elif last_measured_character:`. So Console.print('\x1b[...') or any string that starts with a zero-width char or a lone VS16 hangs forever. A third edge: a trailing ZWJ does `index += 2` and pushes the span end past len(text).
best_solution: Make every branch of the loop consume at least one codepoint and keep the invariant that spans cover every string index with no gaps (callers such as chop_cells/_split_text slice text by span starts/ends). In split_graphemes: (a) if the char is ZWJ or VS16 and there are no spans yet, append a zero-width span (index, index+1, 0) and continue; (b) ZWJ: keep `index += 2` (it swallows the joined next codepoint into the previous grapheme, which the existing family-emoji tests depend on) but clamp to +1 when the ZWJ is the last char; extend spans[-1]; (c) VS16: always `index += 1`; if last_measured_character is set apply the narrow-to-wide +1 width, otherwise just extend spans[-1]; (d) zero-width non-special char: extend spans[-1] if any, else append (index, index+1, 0). Result: '\x1b' -> ([(0,1,0)], 0), '\x1b\x1b' -> ([(0,2,0)], 0), '\u200d\u200d' -> ([(0,2,0)], 0), and chop_cells('\x1b', 3) -> [] because line_size stays 0.
acceptable_alternatives: Any restructuring that guarantees progress on every iteration, keeps ZWJ consuming the following codepoint (index += 2, clamped at end), and emits a leading zero-width span (start, end, 0) that later zero-width chars merge into, rather than silently skipping leading zero-width chars. A plain `index += 1` fallback that drops those chars from the span list fixes the hang but fails the 6 new split_graphemes cases.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py: new test_chop_cells_zero_width parametrized over '', '\x1b', '\x1b\x1b', '\x1b\x1b\x1b', '\x1b\x1b\x1b\x1b' all expecting chop_cells(text, 3) == []. test_split_graphemes gains exact span expectations: '\x1b' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\x1b\x1b' -> [(0,2,0)],0; '\ufe0f' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\ufe0f\ufe0f' -> [(0,2,0)],0; '\u200d' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\u200d\u200d' -> [(0,2,0)],0, and cell_len(text) must agree. Pre-existing test_split_text / test_split_graphemes cases for FM = '\U0001f469\u200d\U0001f527' (width 2, one span (0,3,2)) must keep passing, so the ZWJ += 2 step must not change.
locating_signals: Statement names the function split_graphemes (rich/cells.py) and the symptom 'infinite loop'; the linked issue (not visible to the agent) says the trigger is ANSI escape \x1b returning width 0. Reading the while-loop shows two branches guarded by `elif spans:` / `elif last_measured_character:` with no else, i.e. no index advance.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed. v4 (79 calls) only changed the ZWJ step from += 2 to += 1: breaks ZWJ emoji joining (5 existing test_split_text FM cases fail) and leaves the \x1b hang, so the run times out after 40 tests. v6 also changed ZWJ to += 1 and added `else: index += 1` for zero-width chars with no spans, fixing the \x1b hang but dropping the char (spans [] instead of [(0,1,0)]); it left the VS16-without-previous-char branch non-advancing, so it hangs on '\ufe0f' after 60 tests. v7 only added `else: index += 1` to the VS16 branch; the \x1b leading-zero-width hang remains and the run times out at test 41. v8 fixed all hangs (ZWJ += 1, VS16 always advances, zero-width else index += 1) but produced 14 failures: 8 pre-existing ZWJ/FM cases (family emoji now splits into two width-2 graphemes) and 6 new cases because leading zero-width chars were skipped instead of recorded as (i, i+1, 0) spans; it also left repro.py and reproduce_issue.py in the repo. Common error: the agent mistook the intentional ZWJ `index += 2` for the bug and never ran the existing tests/test_cells.py, which would have caught it.
generalizable_lesson: For an 'infinite loop' fix, find each loop branch that can finish without advancing the cursor (an `elif cond:` with no else) and add the missing advance there. Leave the step sizes of branches that already make progress alone: an unusual step like `+= 2` is usually intentional (here it consumes the joined codepoint). Keep the output's structural invariant, here that spans cover every index, by emitting an empty or zero-weight element instead of silently skipping input. Then run the module's existing test file before finishing. Existing tests would have caught 3 of our 4 regressions.
one_line_solution: Guarantee every split_graphemes branch advances and emits zero-width spans for leading ZWJ/VS16/zero-width chars; keep the ZWJ `+= 2`.

v4_blocker: changed intentional ZWJ step; timed out
flip_note: Existing test_cells.py catches the ZWJ regression in 3 of 4 configs.

root_cause: Console.print() with no positional objects always substituted objects=(NewLine(),), ignoring a custom end. So console.print(end="!") printed "\n" instead of "!". The empty string goes through render_str into the text list, check_text joins it with Text(sep, end=end), and the output is exactly `end` ("!"). Keeping NewLine() for the default end preserves the existing print() -> "\n" behaviour. The rest of the gold diff is cosmetic: it moves `from os import PathLike` into sorted order and reformats the save_text signature. The PR's 'drop Python 3.8' part lives in pyproject/README, is not in the gold source patch and is not tested.

root_cause: FileProxy subclasses io.TextIOBase. It forwards unknown attributes through __getattr__ and already has an explicit fileno(), but isatty() is inherited from io.TextIOBase, which always returns False. Because the name resolves on the MRO, __getattr__ is never reached. The result is that sys.stdout.isatty() inside Live(redirect_stdout=True) returned False even on a real terminal.
best_solution: The statement says 'proxy isatty', and FileProxy is the class in rich whose name contains 'proxy', so the fix goes in rich/file_proxy.py. Add an explicit delegating method next to the existing fileno(): `def isatty(self) -> bool: return self.__file.isatty()`. root_cause: TableDataElement.on_text converted str to Text and then unconditionally called text.stylize(context.current_style) on every chunk, including the already syntax-highlighted Text that MarkdownContext.on_text produces for code_inline tokens when inline_code_lexer/inline_code_theme are set. The whole-range stylize span is appended after the per-token highlight spans, so it overrides them and inline code in table cells renders in the flat markdown.code style (1;36;40) instead of the Pygments theme.
best_solution: Mirror the sibling TextElement.on_text pattern: apply the context style only to plain strings, and append pre-styled Text untouched. In rich/markdown.py TableDataElement.on_text: `if isinstance(text, str): self.content.append(text, context.current_style) else: self.content.append_text(text)`. Reasoning from the title alone: 'inline code' + 'table' points to the code_inline token path and TableDataElement; comparing TableDataElement.on_text against TextElement.on_text (which passes style None for Text) shows the only difference is the blanket stylize, which clobbers highlight spans.
acceptable_alternatives: Any variant that keeps Text chunks' spans intact: Text(text) + stylize only for str then append_text (v6), or Text(text, style=current_style) for str (v7; append_text turns text.style into a span, so it is equivalent). Wrapping the Text in a new style layer UNDER its spans would also work, but stylize_before is unnecessary.
